<div id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p5.1" class="ltx_p">Detailed derivations for <a href="#S2.Thmlemma2" title="Lemma 2.2 (Softmax Aggregator Jacobian). ‣ 2.3 Optimization Dynamics: The Correlation Gradient Bottleneck ‣ 2 Theoretical Analysis of Correlation Learning in Attention-based Aggregation ‣ Breaking the Correlation Plateau: On the Optimization and Capacity Limits of Attention-Based Regressors" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Lemma</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.2</span></a>, <a href="#S2.Thmtheorem1" title="Theorem 2.1 (Gradient of PCC w.r.t. Attention Logits). ‣ 2.3 Optimization Dynamics: The Correlation Gradient Bottleneck ‣ 2 Theoretical Analysis of Correlation Learning in Attention-based Aggregation ‣ Breaking the Correlation Plateau: On the Optimization and Capacity Limits of Attention-Based Regressors" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Theorem</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.1</span></a> are provided in <a href="#A2.SS1" title="B.1 Gradient of Pearson Correlation w.r.t. Attention Logits ‣ Appendix B Gradient Analysis of Correlation ‣ Breaking the Correlation Plateau: On the Optimization and Capacity Limits of Attention-Based Regressors" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.1</span></a>. Proofs for <a href="#S2.Thmlemma3" title="Lemma 2.3 (Gradient of MSE w.r.t. Attention Logits). ‣ 2.3 Optimization Dynamics: The Correlation Gradient Bottleneck ‣ 2 Theoretical Analysis of Correlation Learning in Attention-based Aggregation ‣ Breaking the Correlation Plateau: On the Optimization and Capacity Limits of Attention-Based Regressors" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Lemma</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.3</span></a>, <a href="#S2.Thmcorollary1" title="Corollary 2.1 (PCC/MSE Gradient Ratio Decay). ‣ Gradient Decomposition and the Optimization Conflict. ‣ 2.3 Optimization Dynamics: The Correlation Gradient Bottleneck ‣ 2 Theoretical Analysis of Correlation Learning in Attention-based Aggregation ‣ Breaking the Correlation Plateau: On the Optimization and Capacity Limits of Attention-Based Regressors" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Corollary</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.1</span></a>, and <a href="#S2.Thmcorollary2" title="Corollary 2.2 (PCC Gradient Magnitude Bound). ‣ Gradient Decomposition and the Optimization Conflict. ‣ 2.3 Optimization Dynamics: The Correlation Gradient Bottleneck ‣ 2 Theoretical Analysis of Correlation Learning in Attention-based Aggregation ‣ Breaking the Correlation Plateau: On the Optimization and Capacity Limits of Attention-Based Regressors" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Corollary</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.2</span></a> are provided in <a href="#A3" title="Appendix C Proofs for Optimization Dynamics Analysis ‣ Breaking the Correlation Plateau: On the Optimization and Capacity Limits of Attention-Based Regressors" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.Thmremark3" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_remark">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S2.Thmremark3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Remark 2.3</span></span><span id="S2.Thmremark3.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(The Two Bottlenecks of Softmax Attention for Correlation)<span id="S2.Thmremark3.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S2.Thmremark3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.Thmremark3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.Thmremark3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">The gradient analysis reveals two key bottlenecks in optimization dynamics that drive PCC plateaus:</span></p>
</div>
<div id="S2.Thmremark3.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.Thmremark3.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.Thmremark3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold ltx_font_italic">1. Dominance of the MSE Gradient.<span id="S2.Thmremark3.p2.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">
<a href="#S2.Thmcorollary1" title="Corollary 2.1 (PCC/MSE Gradient Ratio Decay). ‣ Gradient Decomposition and the Optimization Conflict. ‣ 2.3 Optimization Dynamics: The Correlation Gradient Bottleneck ‣ 2 Theoretical Analysis of Correlation Learning in Attention-based Aggregation ‣ Breaking the Correlation Plateau: On the Optimization and Capacity Limits of Attention-Based Regressors" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Corollary</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.1</span></a> reveals a critical conflict in the joint optimization: the ratio of the PCC gradient magnitude relative to the MSE gradient magnitude decays rapidly at a rate of <math id="S2.Thmremark3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{O}(1/\sigma_{\hat{y}}^{3/2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">σ</mi><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="normal">y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{O}(1/\sigma_{\hat{y}}^{3/2})</annotation></semantics></math>. Training with the joint loss minimizes the MSE std-matching term in <a href="#S2.E1" title="In Proposition 2.1 (MSE Mean–std–correlation Decomposition). ‣ 2.2 Preliminaries: The Interplay Between MSE and PCC ‣ 2 Theoretical Analysis of Correlation Learning in Attention-based Aggregation ‣ Breaking the Correlation Plateau: On the Optimization and Capacity Limits of Attention-Based Regressors" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Equation</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>, which drives <math id="S2.Thmremark3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{\hat{y}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">σ</mi><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="normal">y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{\hat{y}}</annotation></semantics></math> toward the target standard deviation <math id="S2.Thmremark3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{y}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">σ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">y</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{y}</annotation></semantics></math>. As <math id="S2.Thmremark3.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{\hat{y}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">σ</mi><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="normal">y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{\hat{y}}</annotation></semantics></math> typically increases during early training (see <a href="#S2.F4" title="In Gradient Decomposition and the Optimization Conflict. ‣ 2.3 Optimization Dynamics: The Correlation Gradient Bottleneck ‣ 2 Theoretical Analysis of Correlation Learning in Attention-based Aggregation ‣ Breaking the Correlation Plateau: On the Optimization and Capacity Limits of Attention-Based Regressors" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>), the relative contribution of the PCC gradient diminishes significantly. Consequently, the optimization becomes dominated by the MSE objective (magnitude matching), effectively downplaying PCC optimization (shape matching) and causing the plateau, even when the PCC loss weight <math id="S2.Thmremark3.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda_{\text{PCC}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">λ</mi><mtext>PCC</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_{\text{PCC}}</annotation></semantics></math> is large. This motivates optimization strategies that counteract this rapid attenuation.</span></span></p>
</div>
<div id="S2.Thmremark3.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.Thmremark3.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.Thmremark3.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold ltx_font_italic">2. Dependence on Within-sample Homogeneity.<span id="S2.Thmremark3.p3.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">
The gradient bound in <a href="#S2.Thmcorollary2" title="Corollary 2.2 (PCC Gradient Magnitude Bound). ‣ Gradient Decomposition and the Optimization Conflict. ‣ 2.3 Optimization Dynamics: The Correlation Gradient Bottleneck ‣ 2 Theoretical Analysis of Correlation Learning in Attention-based Aggregation ‣ Breaking the Correlation Plateau: On the Optimization and Capacity Limits of Attention-Based Regressors" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Corollary</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.2</span></a> is proportional to the in-sample dispersion <math id="S2.Thmremark3.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">σ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{s}</annotation></semantics></math>. When a sample’s elements are homogeneous, <math id="S2.Thmremark3.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">σ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{s}</annotation></semantics></math> is small and the PCC gradient magnitude reduces, effectively hindering improvements to PCC via attention adjustment. Furthermore, since attention scoring functions are generally continuous, homogeneous inputs lead to low-variance logits <math id="S2.Thmremark3.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{si}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">z</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{si}</annotation></semantics></math>. Under fixed-temperature softmax, this results in near-uniform weights <math id="S2.Thmremark3.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha_{si}\!\approx\!1/n_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">α</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0.108em">≈</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha_{si}\!\approx\!1/n_{s}</annotation></semantics></math>, suppressing per-sample selectivity. These effects motivate mechanisms that adapt attention sensitivity to the in-sample dispersion.</span></span></p>
</div>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">2.4 </span>Model Capacity: The PCC Ceiling of Convex Aggregation</h3>

<div id="S2.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Beyond optimization dynamics, we study the limits of the aggregator’s expressivity. Softmax attention performs convex combinations, restricting aggregated embedding <math id="S2.SS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{v}_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐯</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{v}_{s}</annotation></semantics></math> to the convex hull of the in-sample embeddings <math id="S2.SS4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{\mathbf{h}_{si}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>𝐡</mi><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{\mathbf{h}_{si}\}</annotation></semantics></math>. We study how much PCC improvement can be achieved by any convex aggregator over mean-pooling and show a capacity limit governed by in-sample homogeneity.</p>
</div>
<section id="S2.SS4.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Prediction Decompositon.</h5>

<div id="S2.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We decompose the sample embedding <math id="S2.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{v}_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐯</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{v}_{s}</annotation></semantics></math> relative to the mean-pooling embedding <math id="S2.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{\mu}_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝝁</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{\mu}_{s}</annotation></semantics></math>. The prediction can be decomposed as:
<math id="S2.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{y}_{s}=\underbrace{(\mathbf{w}^{\top}\bm{\mu}_{s}+c)}_{\bar{y}_{s}}+\underbrace{\mathbf{w}^{\top}(\mathbf{v}_{s}-\bm{\mu}_{s})}_{\Delta\hat{y}_{s}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><munder><munder accentunder="true"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>𝐰</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝝁</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="true">⏟</mo></munder><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>s</mi></msub></munder><mo>+</mo><munder><munder accentunder="true"><mrow><msup><mi>𝐰</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐯</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>𝝁</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="true">⏟</mo></munder><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>s</mi></msub></mrow></munder></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{y}_{s}=\underbrace{(\mathbf{w}^{\top}\bm{\mu}_{s}+c)}_{\bar{y}_{s}}+\underbrace{\mathbf{w}^{\top}(\mathbf{v}_{s}-\bm{\mu}_{s})}_{\Delta\hat{y}_{s}}</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="S2.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{y}_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{y}_{s}</annotation></semantics></math> is the prediction using mean-pooling aggregation, and <math id="S2.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta\hat{y}_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>s</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta\hat{y}_{s}</annotation></semantics></math> is the attention-induced perturbation.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.Thmtheorem2" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_theorem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S2.Thmtheorem2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem 2.2</span></span><span id="S2.Thmtheorem2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(PCC Gain Bound for Convex Attention)<span id="S2.Thmtheorem2.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S2.Thmtheorem2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.Thmtheorem2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.Thmtheorem2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="S2.Thmtheorem2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{0}:=\operatorname{std}_{s}(\bar{y}_{s})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>σ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>:=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>std</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>s</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{0}:=\operatorname{std}_{s}(\bar{y}_{s})</annotation></semantics></math> be the standard deviation of the mean-pooling predictions; define baseline <math id="S2.Thmtheorem2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho_{0}:=\operatorname{PCC}(\mathbf{y},\bar{\mathbf{y}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>:=</mo><mrow><mi>PCC</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐲</mi><mo>,</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐲</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho_{0}:=\operatorname{PCC}(\mathbf{y},\bar{\mathbf{y}})</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S2.Thmtheorem2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ρ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho</annotation></semantics></math> is the PCC after applying any convex attention mechanism. Provided <math id="S2.Thmtheorem2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|\mathbf{w}\|_{2}&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>𝐰</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\mathbf{w}\|_{2}&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S2.Thmtheorem2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{R}&lt;\sigma_{0}/\|\mathbf{w}\|_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>R</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo>&lt;</mo><mrow><msub><mi>σ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>/</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>𝐰</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{R}&lt;\sigma_{0}/\|\mathbf{w}\|_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>,</span></p>
<table id="S2.EGx3" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S2.E8"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S2.E8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle|\rho-\rho_{0}|\ \leq\ \frac{2\,\tilde{R}}{\sigma_{0}/\|\mathbf{w}\|_{2}-\tilde{R}}." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow><mo rspace="0.500em" stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.778em">≤</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>R</mi><mo>~</mo></mover></mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>σ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>/</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>𝐰</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo>−</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>R</mi><mo>~</mo></mover></mrow></mfrac></mstyle></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle|\rho-\rho_{0}|\ \leq\ \frac{2\,\tilde{R}}{\sigma_{0}/\|\mathbf{w}\|_{2}-\tilde{R}}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>

</table>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Detailed proof is provided in <a href="#A4" title="Appendix D Achievable PCC Bound of Convex Attention Models ‣ Breaking the Correlation Plateau: On the Optimization and Capacity Limits of Attention-Based Regressors" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">D</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.Thmremark4" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_remark">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S2.Thmremark4.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Remark 2.4</span></span><span id="S2.Thmremark4.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S2.Thmremark4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.Thmremark4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><a href="#S2.Thmtheorem2" title="Theorem 2.2 (PCC Gain Bound for Convex Attention). ‣ Prediction Decompositon. ‣ 2.4 Model Capacity: The PCC Ceiling of Convex Aggregation ‣ 2 Theoretical Analysis of Correlation Learning in Attention-based Aggregation ‣ Breaking the Correlation Plateau: On the Optimization and Capacity Limits of Attention-Based Regressors" class="ltx_ref ltx_font_italic"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Theorem</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.2</span></a><span id="S2.Thmremark4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> shows that the PCC improvement bound of any convex attention depends only on the ratio between convex hull radius <math id="S2.Thmremark4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{R}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>R</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{R}</annotation></semantics></math> (reflecting in-sample homogeneity) and the normalized standard deviation of mean-pooling baseline (<math id="S2.Thmremark4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{0}/\|\mathbf{w}\|_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>σ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>/</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>𝐰</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{0}/\|\mathbf{w}\|_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>). The bound is scale-invariant and independent of the regression head magnitude since <math id="S2.Thmremark4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{0}/\|\mathbf{w}\|_{2}=\operatorname{std}_{s}(\mathbf{w}^{\top}\bm{\mu}_{s})/\|\mathbf{w}\|_{2}=\operatorname{std}_{s}\!\big((\mathbf{w}^{\top}/\|\mathbf{w}\|_{2})\bm{\mu}_{s}\big)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>σ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>/</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>𝐰</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>std</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>𝐰</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝛍</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>/</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>𝐰</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>std</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>𝐰</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo>/</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>𝐰</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝛍</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{0}/\|\mathbf{w}\|_{2}=\operatorname{std}_{s}(\mathbf{w}^{\top}\bm{\mu}_{s})/\|\mathbf{w}\|_{2}=\operatorname{std}_{s}\!\big((\mathbf{w}^{\top}/\|\mathbf{w}\|_{2})\bm{\mu}_{s}\big)</annotation></semantics></math>. When in-sample homogeneity is high (<math id="S2.Thmremark4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{R}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>R</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{R}</annotation></semantics></math> is small), no convex attention can substantially increase correlation. The limitation arises because <math id="S2.Thmremark4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{v}_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐯</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{v}_{s}</annotation></semantics></math> is confined to the convex hull; a small hull restricts the magnitude of adjustments to the aggregated embedding, thereby limiting the potential PCC improvement and motivating mechanisms that can extrapolate beyond it.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">2.5 </span>Summary of Theoretical Insights</h3>

<div id="S2.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Our analysis reveals that the difficulty of optimizing PCC using softmax attention stems from two aspects: optimization dynamics and model capacity. <a href="#S2.Thmremark3" title="Remark 2.3 (The Two Bottlenecks of Softmax Attention for Correlation). ‣ Gradient Decomposition and the Optimization Conflict. ‣ 2.3 Optimization Dynamics: The Correlation Gradient Bottleneck ‣ 2 Theoretical Analysis of Correlation Learning in Attention-based Aggregation ‣ Breaking the Correlation Plateau: On the Optimization and Capacity Limits of Attention-Based Regressors" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Remark</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.3</span></a> highlights the vanishing PCC gradients due to cross-sample dispersion attenuation <math id="S2.SS5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1/\sigma_{\hat{y}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><msub><mi>σ</mi><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1/\sigma_{\hat{y}}</annotation></semantics></math> and weak in-sample dispersion. <a href="#S2.Thmremark4" title="Remark 2.4. ‣ Prediction Decompositon. ‣ 2.4 Model Capacity: The PCC Ceiling of Convex Aggregation ‣ 2 Theoretical Analysis of Correlation Learning in Attention-based Aggregation ‣ Breaking the Correlation Plateau: On the Optimization and Capacity Limits of Attention-Based Regressors" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Remark</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.4</span></a> further shows that any convex aggregator is restricted to the convex hull, which limits the possible PCC gain by ratio <math id="S2.SS5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{R}/(\sigma_{0}/\|\mathbf{w}\|_{2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>R</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo>/</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>σ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>/</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>𝐰</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{R}/(\sigma_{0}/\|\mathbf{w}\|_{2})</annotation></semantics></math>. Together, these effects explain the plateau and motivate a novel attention mechanism proposed in the next section that addresses the identified bottlenecks accordingly.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S3" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">3 </span>Extrapolative Correlation Attention (ECA)</h2>

<div id="S3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Our analysis has identified fundamental limitations in softmax attention for optimizing joint MSE+PCC objective. To address these issues, we propose Extrapolative Correlation Attention (ECA), a novel drop-in attention module for regression that enhances both optimization and expressivity. ECA incorporates three components: (i) Scaled Residual Aggregation to break the convex hull constraint; (ii) Dispersion-Aware Temperature Softmax, to avoid gradient collapse; and (iii) Dispersion-Normalized PCC Loss, which compensates the <math id="S3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1/\sigma_{\hat{y}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><msub><mi>σ</mi><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1/\sigma_{\hat{y}}</annotation></semantics></math> attenuation in correlation gradients.</p>
</div>
<section id="S3.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.1 </span>Breaking the Convex Hull with Scaled Residual Aggregation (SRA)</h3>

<div id="S3.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><a href="#S2.Thmtheorem2" title="Theorem 2.2 (PCC Gain Bound for Convex Attention). ‣ Prediction Decompositon. ‣ 2.4 Model Capacity: The PCC Ceiling of Convex Aggregation ‣ 2 Theoretical Analysis of Correlation Learning in Attention-based Aggregation ‣ Breaking the Correlation Plateau: On the Optimization and Capacity Limits of Attention-Based Regressors" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Theorem</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.2</span></a> shows that any convex attention mechanism is capacity-limited in correlation improvement because the aggregated embedding <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{v}_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐯</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{v}_{s}</annotation></semantics></math> lies inside the convex hull of the in-sample embeddings <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{\mathbf{h}_{si}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>𝐡</mi><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{\mathbf{h}_{si}\}</annotation></semantics></math>. This PCC gain bound is especially tighter when in-sample dispersion is low. To relax this limit, we introduce Scaled Residual Aggregation (SRA): instead of a strict convex aggregation, the model extrapolates along the residual <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\mathbf{h}_{si}-\bm{\mu}_{s})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐡</mi><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>𝝁</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\mathbf{h}_{si}-\bm{\mu}_{s})</annotation></semantics></math>, allowing <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{v}_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐯</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{v}_{s}</annotation></semantics></math> to move beyond the convex hull.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Given the mean embedding <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\bm{\mu}_{s}=1/n_{s}\sum_{i}\mathbf{h}_{si}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝝁</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>n</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>∑</mo><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>i</mi></msub><mi>𝐡</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{\mu}_{s}=1/n_{s}\sum_{i}\mathbf{h}_{si}</annotation></semantics></math>, we define the residual <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta\mathbf{v}_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐯</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta\mathbf{v}_{s}</annotation></semantics></math> as the attention-weighted deviation from the mean: <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta\mathbf{v}_{s}:=\sum_{i}\alpha_{si}(\mathbf{h}_{si}-\bm{\mu}_{s})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐯</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">:=</mo><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>i</mi></msub><mrow><msub><mi>α</mi><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐡</mi><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>𝝁</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta\mathbf{v}_{s}:=\sum_{i}\alpha_{si}(\mathbf{h}_{si}-\bm{\mu}_{s})</annotation></semantics></math>. SRA scales this residual by a learnable factor <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma_{s}\geq 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>γ</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma_{s}\geq 1</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<table id="S3.E9" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{v}_{s}^{\text{ECA}}\;=\;\bm{\mu}_{s}\;+\;\gamma_{s}\cdot\Delta\mathbf{v}_{s}\;=\;\bm{\mu}_{s}\;+\;\gamma_{s}\sum_{i}\alpha_{si}\bigl(\mathbf{h}_{si}-\bm{\mu}_{s}\bigr)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>𝐯</mi><mi>s</mi><mtext>ECA</mtext></msubsup><mo lspace="0.558em" rspace="0.558em">=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝝁</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.502em">+</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>γ</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐯</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.558em">=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝝁</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.502em">+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>γ</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mi>i</mi></munder><mrow><msub><mi>α</mi><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐡</mi><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>𝝁</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{v}_{s}^{\text{ECA}}\;=\;\bm{\mu}_{s}\;+\;\gamma_{s}\cdot\Delta\mathbf{v}_{s}\;=\;\bm{\mu}_{s}\;+\;\gamma_{s}\sum_{i}\alpha_{si}\bigl(\mathbf{h}_{si}-\bm{\mu}_{s}\bigr).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(9)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">We parameterize <math id="S3.SS1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>γ</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma_{s}</annotation></semantics></math> using a small, sample-specific MLP conditioned on the mean embedding <math id="S3.SS1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{\mu}_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝝁</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{\mu}_{s}</annotation></semantics></math> and use a shifted Softplus activation to ensure <math id="S3.SS1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma_{s}\geq 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>γ</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma_{s}\geq 1</annotation></semantics></math>, that is <math id="S3.SS1.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma_{s}=1+\operatorname{Softplus}(\operatorname{MLP}_{\theta_{\gamma}}(\bm{\mu}_{s}))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>γ</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>Softplus</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>MLP</mi><msub><mi>θ</mi><mi>γ</mi></msub></msub><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝝁</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma_{s}=1+\operatorname{Softplus}(\operatorname{MLP}_{\theta_{\gamma}}(\bm{\mu}_{s}))</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">The factor <math id="S3.SS1.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>γ</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma_{s}</annotation></semantics></math> allows the model to amplify weak in-sample contrasts. When <math id="S3.SS1.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma_{s}=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>γ</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma_{s}=1</annotation></semantics></math>, SRA reduces to standard convex attention aggregation. For <math id="S3.SS1.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma_{s}&gt;1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>γ</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma_{s}&gt;1</annotation></semantics></math>, the model extrapolates beyond the convex hull, and more importantly, it breaks the convexity constraint. In standard attention, the deviation <math id="S3.SS1.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|\Delta\mathbf{v}_{s}\|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐯</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\Delta\mathbf{v}_{s}\|</annotation></semantics></math>is bounded by the radius of the convex hull <math id="S3.SS1.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{s}</annotation></semantics></math>. SRA expands the reachable space by increasing the effective radius and fundamentally bypasses the capacity limit derived for convex aggregators in <a href="#S2.Thmtheorem2" title="Theorem 2.2 (PCC Gain Bound for Convex Attention). ‣ Prediction Decompositon. ‣ 2.4 Model Capacity: The PCC Ceiling of Convex Aggregation ‣ 2 Theoretical Analysis of Correlation Learning in Attention-based Aggregation ‣ Breaking the Correlation Plateau: On the Optimization and Capacity Limits of Attention-Based Regressors" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Theorem</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.2</span></a>. In practice we optionally clip <math id="S3.SS1.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>γ</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma_{s}</annotation></semantics></math> at a maximum (e.g., <math id="S3.SS1.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma_{\text{max}}=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>γ</mi><mtext>max</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma_{\text{max}}=2</annotation></semantics></math>) or add a regularizer <math id="S3.SS1.p4.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\gamma}=\tfrac{\lambda_{\gamma}}{S}\sum_{s}(\gamma_{s}-1)^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mi>γ</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>γ</mi></msub><mi>S</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><msub><mo rspace="0em">∑</mo><mi>s</mi></msub><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>γ</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\gamma}=\tfrac{\lambda_{\gamma}}{S}\sum_{s}(\gamma_{s}-1)^{2}</annotation></semantics></math> to discourage excessive scaling.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.2 </span>Dispersion-Aware Temperature Softmax (DATS)</h3>

<div id="S3.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">While SRA enables extrapolation beyond the convex hull, the model still needs a informative direction to extrapolate. In homogeneous samples, standard softmax produces flat attention <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha_{si}\!\approx\!1/n_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>α</mi><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0.108em">≈</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha_{si}\!\approx\!1/n_{s}</annotation></semantics></math> (<a href="#S2.Thmremark3" title="Remark 2.3 (The Two Bottlenecks of Softmax Attention for Correlation). ‣ Gradient Decomposition and the Optimization Conflict. ‣ 2.3 Optimization Dynamics: The Correlation Gradient Bottleneck ‣ 2 Theoretical Analysis of Correlation Learning in Attention-based Aggregation ‣ Breaking the Correlation Plateau: On the Optimization and Capacity Limits of Attention-Based Regressors" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Remark</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.3</span></a>), which pulls the aggregated embedding toward <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{\mu}_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝝁</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{\mu}_{s}</annotation></semantics></math> and makes the residual in <a href="#S3.E9" title="In 3.1 Breaking the Convex Hull with Scaled Residual Aggregation (SRA) ‣ 3 Extrapolative Correlation Attention (ECA) ‣ Breaking the Correlation Plateau: On the Optimization and Capacity Limits of Attention-Based Regressors" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Equation</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a> small (<math id="S3.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta\mathbf{v}_{s}\!\approx\!0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐯</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></mrow><mo>≈</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta\mathbf{v}_{s}\!\approx\!0</annotation></semantics></math>). With small residual, SRA provides little benefit. To address this, we introduce Dispersion-Aware Temperature Softmax (DATS), which adapts the attention temperature to the in-sample dispersion, sharpening attention when homogeneity is high:</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We modify the softmax attention for <a href="#S3.E9" title="In 3.1 Breaking the Convex Hull with Scaled Residual Aggregation (SRA) ‣ 3 Extrapolative Correlation Attention (ECA) ‣ Breaking the Correlation Plateau: On the Optimization and Capacity Limits of Attention-Based Regressors" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Equation</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a> with a sample-specific temperature <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>τ</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau_{s}</annotation></semantics></math> reflecting within-sample dispersion:</p>
<table id="S3.EGx4" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S3.E10"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\alpha_{si}=\operatorname{softmax}\!\left(\frac{z_{si}}{\tau_{s}}\right),\quad\tau_{s}=T_{\min}+\beta\sqrt{\frac{1}{n_{s}}\sum_{1\leq i\leq n_{s}}\|\mathbf{h}_{si}-\bm{\mu}_{s}\|^{2}}." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>α</mi><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mpadded style="width:3.720em;" width="3.720em"><mi>softmax</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><msub><mi>z</mi><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><msub><mi>τ</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></mfrac></mstyle><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>τ</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>min</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msqrt><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>≤</mo><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></mrow></munder></mstyle><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐡</mi><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>𝝁</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mrow></msqrt></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\alpha_{si}=\operatorname{softmax}\!\left(\frac{z_{si}}{\tau_{s}}\right),\quad\tau_{s}=T_{\min}+\beta\sqrt{\frac{1}{n_{s}}\sum_{1\leq i\leq n_{s}}\|\mathbf{h}_{si}-\bm{\mu}_{s}\|^{2}}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(10)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Here <math id="S3.SS2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{\min}\!&gt;\!0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>min</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.108em">&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{\min}\!&gt;\!0</annotation></semantics></math> lower-bounds the temperature for stability, and <math id="S3.SS2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta\geq 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta\geq 0</annotation></semantics></math> is a hyperparameter that controls sensitivity. When embeddings within a sample are homogeneous, <math id="S3.SS2.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>τ</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau_{s}</annotation></semantics></math> has lower value so small differences between logits <math id="S3.SS2.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{si}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>z</mi><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{si}</annotation></semantics></math> become sharper after attention, yielding a meaningful deviation <math id="S3.SS2.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta\mathbf{v}_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐯</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta\mathbf{v}_{s}</annotation></semantics></math> that SRA can effectively amplify.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.3 </span>Stabilizing Optimization: Dispersion-Normalized PCC Loss (DNPL)</h3>

<div id="S3.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><a href="#S2.Thmtheorem1" title="Theorem 2.1 (Gradient of PCC w.r.t. Attention Logits). ‣ 2.3 Optimization Dynamics: The Correlation Gradient Bottleneck ‣ 2 Theoretical Analysis of Correlation Learning in Attention-based Aggregation ‣ Breaking the Correlation Plateau: On the Optimization and Capacity Limits of Attention-Based Regressors" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Theorem</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.1</span></a> shows that the correlation gradient is attenuated by <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1/\sigma_{\hat{y}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><msub><mi>σ</mi><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1/\sigma_{\hat{y}}</annotation></semantics></math>. As MSE optimization improves standard deviation matching, <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{\hat{y}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>σ</mi><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{\hat{y}}</annotation></semantics></math> increases, which shrinks the PCC gradient and contributes to a PCC plateau. We counteract this attenuation effect with a Dispersion-Normalized PCC Loss (DNPL), which rescales the PCC term by the current prediction standard deviation while blocking its gradient:</p>
<table id="S3.E11" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E11.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{\mathcal{L}}_{\text{PCC}}=\operatorname{StopGrad}(\sigma_{\hat{y}})\cdot(1-\rho)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mtext>PCC</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>StopGrad</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>σ</mi><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></msub><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>ρ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{\mathcal{L}}_{\text{PCC}}=\operatorname{StopGrad}(\sigma_{\hat{y}})\cdot(1-\rho).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(11)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\operatorname{StopGrad}(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>StopGrad</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\operatorname{StopGrad}(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math> operation ensures we only adjust the gradient magnitude to counteract the attenuation, while leaving the learning objective’s stationary points unchanged.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.4 </span>Overall Objective</h3>

<div id="S3.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The complete ECA framework, including SRA and DATS, is fully differentiable and can be trained end-to-end. The overall learning objective combines the primary regression loss (MSE), the normalized PCC loss (DNPL), and the extrapolation regularizer:</p>
<table id="S3.E12" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E12.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\text{Total}}=\mathcal{L}_{\text{MSE}}+\lambda_{\text{PCC}}\cdot\tilde{\mathcal{L}}_{\text{PCC}}+\mathcal{L}_{\gamma}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>Total</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>MSE</mtext></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mtext>PCC</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mtext>PCC</mtext></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mi>γ</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\text{Total}}=\mathcal{L}_{\text{MSE}}+\lambda_{\text{PCC}}\cdot\tilde{\mathcal{L}}_{\text{PCC}}+\mathcal{L}_{\gamma}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(12)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">4 </span>Related Works</h2>

<div id="S4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Correlation Learning and Optimization.</span>
Correlation is a core metric in biological and medical areas <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">Langfelder and Horvath, 2008</a>; <a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lawrence and Lin, 1989</a>)</cite>. In these domains, PCC is a standard criterion for evaluating regression performance <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kudrat et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">Long et al., 2023</a>)</cite>. Because PCC is differentiable, it is often optimized directly as a loss in regression pipelines <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kudrat et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib19" title="" class="ltx_ref">Avants et al., 2008</a>)</cite>. From a multi-task perspective, many works combine PCC with MSE to balance the prediction magnitude and shape <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yang et al., 2023</a>; <a href="#bib.bib17" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al., 2022</a>; <a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">Balakrishnan et al., 2019</a>)</cite>. However, the interaction dynamics between MSE and PCC under joint optimization remain underexplored, motivating our analysis of gradient coupling and the observed PCC plateau.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Softmax Attention Aggregation.</span>
Softmax attention is a cornerstone component in the backbones of many representative regression models <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib20" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhou et al., 2021</a>; <a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gorishniy et al., 2021</a>; <a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kim et al., 2019</a>)</cite>. Despite its empirical success, recent theory has revealed expressivity limits of softmax mappings in related contexts <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yang et al., 2017</a>; <a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kanai et al., 2018</a>; <a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">Bhojanapalli et al., 2020</a>)</cite>. However, to our knowledge, no prior work analyzes the model capacity of softmax attention in terms of upper bounds on achievable PCC improvements, especially with high in-sample homogeneity data.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">5 </span>Experiments</h2>

<div id="S5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We evaluate our ECA on four settings, including the challenging high in-sample homogeneity tasks. The evaluations consist of: (i) a synthetic regression dataset with controllable in-sample homogeneity; (ii) three representative tabular regression benchmarks from the UCI ML Repository <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib41" title="" class="ltx_ref">Asuncion et al., 2007</a>)</cite>; (iii) a clinical pathology dataset for spatial transcriptomic prediction, where nearby regions exhibit <em id="S5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">high homogeneity</em>; and (iv) a multimodal sentiment analysis (MSA) dataset, where consecutive video frames are <em id="S5.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">highly homogeneous</em>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">As ECA is a drop-in replacement for softmax attention, we integrate it into existing attention-based regression models for each benchmark to measure the performance improvement. More details are provided in <a href="#A7" title="Appendix G Detailed Experimental Settings ‣ Breaking the Correlation Plateau: On the Optimization and Capacity Limits of Attention-Based Regressors" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">G</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<section id="S5.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.1 </span>Experimental Setup</h3>

<div id="S5.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Synthetic Dataset.</span> We construct a synthetic dataset to validate our theory and proposed ECA method. We synthetic <math id="S5.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> samples, each with <math id="S5.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> element embeddings in <math id="S5.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>D</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D</annotation></semantics></math> dimensions as input samples. In each sample, one key element carries signal along a fixed unit direction <math id="S5.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{w}^{\ast}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>𝐰</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{w}^{\ast}</annotation></semantics></math>, while the remaining <math id="S5.SS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K\!-\!1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo lspace="0.052em">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K\!-\!1</annotation></semantics></math> background elements cluster around a shared sample mean. The label <math id="S5.SS1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{y}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐲</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{y}</annotation></semantics></math> is the projection of the sample mean onto <math id="S5.SS1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{w}^{\ast}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>𝐰</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{w}^{\ast}</annotation></semantics></math> with a term proportional to the key strength and small additive noise. We control within-sample homogeneity via <math id="S5.SS1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>η</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta</annotation></semantics></math> (larger <math id="S5.SS1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>η</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta</annotation></semantics></math> means the key deviates further from the mean), yielding four homogeneity levels <math id="S5.SS1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{\sigma}\in\{0.10,0.24,0.42,0.73\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>σ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0.10</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.24</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.42</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.73</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{\sigma}\in\{0.10,0.24,0.42,0.73\}</annotation></semantics></math> where lower <math id="S5.SS1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{\sigma}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>σ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{\sigma}</annotation></semantics></math> indicates higher homogeneity. We compare regression model with one layer of ECA to one layer of standard softmax attention and report MSE and PCC.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">UCI ML Repository Datasets.</span> We evaluate on three representative tabular regression benchmarks: Appliance Energy Prediction (28 features, 1 target) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib42" title="" class="ltx_ref">Candanedo, 2017</a>)</cite>, Online News Popularity (58 features, 1 target) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">Fernandes et al., 2015</a>)</cite>, and Superconductivity (81 features, 1 target) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib44" title="" class="ltx_ref">Hamidieh, 2018</a>)</cite>. We integrate ECA into the attention layer of the FT-Transformer <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gorishniy et al., 2021</a>)</cite> and report mean absolute error (MAE), MSE, and PCC.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Spatial Transcriptomic Dataset.</span> We test spatial transcriptomics prediction from pathology images on the 10xProteomic dataset <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib26" title="" class="ltx_ref">Genomics, 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yang et al., 2023</a>)</cite>, which contains <math id="S5.SS1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="32,032" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>32,032</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">32,032</annotation></semantics></math> slide-image patches paired with gene-expression measurements of breast-cancer slides. We follow the data processing and experimental settings of the EGN baseline <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yang et al., 2023</a>)</cite>, which jointly optimize MSE+PCC loss. We adopt ECA methods onto the EGN baseline and report MSE, PCC@F, PCC@S, and PCC@M as evaluation metrics. The training set exhibits high in-sample embedding homogeneity with <math id="S5.SS1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{\sigma}=0.068" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>σ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mn>0.068</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{\sigma}=0.068</annotation></semantics></math> versus cross-sample <math id="S5.SS1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{0}=0.164" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>σ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.164</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{0}=0.164</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS1.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS1.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Multimodal Sentiment Analysis (MSA) Dataset.</span> We use MOSI <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib30" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zadeh et al., 2016</a>)</cite>, a standard MSA benchmark consists of <math id="S5.SS1.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2,199" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2,199</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2,199</annotation></semantics></math> monologue video clips with audio and visual inputs. As illustrated in <a href="#S1.F1" title="In 1 Introduction ‣ Breaking the Correlation Plateau: On the Optimization and Capacity Limits of Attention-Based Regressors" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>, consecutive frames within a clip are more similar than frames across clips. Quantitatively, the video frames shows strong within-sample homogeneity with <math id="S5.SS1.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{\sigma}=0.098" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>σ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mn>0.098</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{\sigma}=0.098</annotation></semantics></math> versus cross-sample <math id="S5.SS1.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{0}=0.170" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>σ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.170</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{0}=0.170</annotation></semantics></math>. We follow the commonly used MOSI processing protocol from THUIAR releases <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib29" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yu et al., 2020</a>; <a href="#bib.bib28" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yu et al., 2021</a>)</cite>. Video frame embeddings are extracted with OpenFace <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib45" title="" class="ltx_ref">Amos et al., 2016</a>)</cite>. Consistent with prior work, we report F1, PCC, and MAE as evaluation metrics. We include 10 representative baselines. ALMT <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib38" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhang et al., 2023</a>)</cite>, the leading baseline optimizing with MSE loss, is selected to incorporate the ECA method.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.T1" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 1: </span>Results on three UCI tabular regression tasks. “ +ECA ” denotes adding ECA onto the FT-Transformer baseline. Rows marked “w/o SRA/DATS/DNPL” are ablation studies that remove the corresponding ECA components. “w/o” = “without” and <span id="S5.T1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">bold</span> indicating best result.</figcaption>

<section id="S5.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.2 </span>Results and analysis</h3>

<div id="S5.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Synthetic Dataset.</span> <a href="#S5.F5" title="In 5.1 Experimental Setup ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ Breaking the Correlation Plateau: On the Optimization and Capacity Limits of Attention-Based Regressors" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> shows case studies on the training and validation curves under different in-sample dispersion (with <math id="S5.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{\sigma}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>σ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{\sigma}</annotation></semantics></math> = 0.10, 0.24, 0.42, and 0.73). The horizontal line indicates the PCC achieved by mean-pooling over input embeddings. This result confirms our theoretical study in three ways: 1) as the homogeneity intensifies, both the PCC of our ECA and baseline model decrease and the MSE get higher (task harder), and the achievable PCC improvement of convex (<em id="S5.SS2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">e.g.</em>, softmax) attention over mean-pooling decreases (<a href="#S2.Thmtheorem2" title="Theorem 2.2 (PCC Gain Bound for Convex Attention). ‣ Prediction Decompositon. ‣ 2.4 Model Capacity: The PCC Ceiling of Convex Aggregation ‣ 2 Theoretical Analysis of Correlation Learning in Attention-based Aggregation ‣ Breaking the Correlation Plateau: On the Optimization and Capacity Limits of Attention-Based Regressors" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Theorem</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.2</span></a>). 2) ECA consistently outperforms standard attention in both PCC and MSE across all four <math id="S5.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{\sigma}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>σ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{\sigma}</annotation></semantics></math>s, achieving PCC gains of <math id="S5.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4.80\%,5.76\%,4.68\%,3.05\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>4.80</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mn>5.76</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mn>4.68</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mn>3.05</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4.80\%,5.76\%,4.68\%,3.05\%</annotation></semantics></math> and MSE reductions of <math id="S5.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="20.3\%,40.8\%,54.0\%,66.7\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>20.3</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mn>40.8</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mn>54.0</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mn>66.7</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">20.3\%,40.8\%,54.0\%,66.7\%</annotation></semantics></math> (in order of increasing <math id="S5.SS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{\sigma}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>σ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{\sigma}</annotation></semantics></math>), showing its ability to explore beyond the convex hull and improving the PCC without compromising the MSE. 3) The PCC curve of ECA keeps improving and converges later and at a higher value than the standard attention baseline, indicating the effectiveness of our proposed DNPL in mitigating the PCC attenuation effect identified in <a href="#S2.Thmremark3" title="Remark 2.3 (The Two Bottlenecks of Softmax Attention for Correlation). ‣ Gradient Decomposition and the Optimization Conflict. ‣ 2.3 Optimization Dynamics: The Correlation Gradient Bottleneck ‣ 2 Theoretical Analysis of Correlation Learning in Attention-based Aggregation ‣ Breaking the Correlation Plateau: On the Optimization and Capacity Limits of Attention-Based Regressors" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Remark</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.3</span></a>.</p>
</div>

</figure>
<div id="S5.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">UCI ML Repository Datasets.</span> Across three UCI tabular regression tasks, adapting our ECA module into the FT-Transformer yields consistent improvements in both magnitude (MSE and MAE) and shape (PCC) metrics. On Appliance, PCC increases by 0.042 and MSE decreases by <math id="S5.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.318\times 10^{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.318</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.318\times 10^{3}</annotation></semantics></math>; on Online News, PCC increases <math id="S5.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.012" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.012</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.012</annotation></semantics></math> from <math id="S5.SS2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.408" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.408</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.408</annotation></semantics></math> while MSE decreases <math id="S5.SS2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.012" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.012</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.012</annotation></semantics></math> from <math id="S5.SS2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.724" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.724</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.724</annotation></semantics></math>; on Superconductivity, PCC <math id="S5.SS2.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.920\!\to\!0.930" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0.930</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.920\!\to\!0.930</annotation></semantics></math> and MSE <math id="S5.SS2.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.772\times 10^{2}\!\to\!1.582\times 10^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>1.772</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mn>1.582</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.772\times 10^{2}\!\to\!1.582\times 10^{2}</annotation></semantics></math>. MAE also decreases across all datasets. These improvements provide strong evidence that addressing our identified PCC gradient limitation and the convex attention capacity limit substantially mitigates the PCC plateau without compromising MSE. The ablations further support the contribution of each components: removing DATS lowers Appliance PCC to <math id="S5.SS2.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.561" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.561</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.561</annotation></semantics></math>, while removing SRA reduces Online News PCC to <math id="S5.SS2.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.418" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.418</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.418</annotation></semantics></math> and removing DNPL decreases Superconductivity PCC to <math id="S5.SS2.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.922" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.922</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.922</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Spatial Transcriptomic Dataset.</span> We follow the EGN <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yang et al., 2023</a>)</cite> setting and report three-fold results. <a href="#S5.F6" title="In 5.2 Results and analysis ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ Breaking the Correlation Plateau: On the Optimization and Capacity Limits of Attention-Based Regressors" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> plots PCC and MSE curves for training and validation. Across all folds, integrating ECA consistently improves both metrics. In fold 2, the EGN baseline’s PCC flattens near epoch 4, but the MSE keeps decreasing, indicating a clear PCC plateau. In contrast, PCC of EGN+ECA continues to increase, effectively breaking the PCC plateau and improving final validation PCC by <math id="S5.SS2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sim 16.51\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mn>16.51</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sim 16.51\%</annotation></semantics></math>. The same pattern holds in folds 0 and 1. Throughout training, EGN+ECA also achieves comparable or lower MSE than EGN alone, indicating that ECA successfully preserves magnitude information while achieving better PCC. <a href="#S5.T3" title="In 5.2 Results and analysis ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ Breaking the Correlation Plateau: On the Optimization and Capacity Limits of Attention-Based Regressors" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> summarizes the overall performance, where EGN+ECA achieves <math id="S5.SS2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+14.64\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mn>14.64</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+14.64\%</annotation></semantics></math> for PCC@F, <math id="S5.SS2.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+11.89\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mn>11.89</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+11.89\%</annotation></semantics></math> for PCC@S, <math id="S5.SS2.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+13.81\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mn>13.81</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+13.81\%</annotation></semantics></math> for PCC@M, and a <math id="S5.SS2.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="9.83\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>9.83</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">9.83\%</annotation></semantics></math> reduction in MSE, showing that ECA effectively and robustly alleviates the PCC plateau without compromising the MSE.</p>
</div>
