stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub></mfrac></mstyle><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="true">⏟</mo></munder><msub><mi>T</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></munder></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\leq\underbrace{\left|(\hat{\mathbf{a}}\cdot\mathbf{b})\left(\frac{1}{|\mathbf{b}+\bm{\delta}|_{2}}-\frac{1}{|\mathbf{b}|_{2}}\right)\right|}_{T_{1}}+\underbrace{\left|\frac{\hat{\mathbf{a}}\cdot\bm{\delta}}{|\mathbf{b}+\bm{\delta}|_{2}}\right|}_{T_{2}}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(95)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A4.Thmlemma2.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.Thmlemma2.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.Thmlemma2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text">We analyze each term. For <math id="A4.Thmlemma2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>T</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, by Cauchy–Schwarz (<math id="A4.Thmlemma2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|\hat{\mathbf{a}}\cdot\bm{\delta}|\leq\|\bm{\delta}\|_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐚</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mi>𝜹</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>𝜹</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|\hat{\mathbf{a}}\cdot\bm{\delta}|\leq\|\bm{\delta}\|_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>) and the reverse triangle inequality (<math id="A4.Thmlemma2.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|\mathbf{b}+\bm{\delta}\|_{2}\geq\|\mathbf{b}\|_{2}-\|\bm{\delta}\|_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>𝐛</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>𝜹</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>≥</mo><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>𝐛</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>𝜹</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\mathbf{b}+\bm{\delta}\|_{2}\geq\|\mathbf{b}\|_{2}-\|\bm{\delta}\|_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>), we have
<math id="A4.Thmlemma2.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{2}\leq\frac{\|\bm{\delta}\|_{2}}{\|\mathbf{b}\|_{2}-\|\bm{\delta}\|_{2}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>T</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>≤</mo><mfrac><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>𝜹</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>𝐛</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>𝜹</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{2}\leq\frac{\|\bm{\delta}\|_{2}}{\|\mathbf{b}\|_{2}-\|\bm{\delta}\|_{2}}</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A4.Thmlemma2.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.Thmlemma2.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.Thmlemma2.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text">For <math id="A4.Thmlemma2.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>T</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{1}</annotation></semantics></math>, we rewrite the expression:
<math id="A4.Thmlemma2.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{1}=|\hat{\mathbf{a}}\cdot\mathbf{b}|\,\left|\frac{\|\mathbf{b}\|_{2}-\|\mathbf{b}+\bm{\delta}\|_{2}}{\|\mathbf{b}\|_{2}\,\|\mathbf{b}+\bm{\delta}\|_{2}}\right|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>T</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐚</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mi>𝐛</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>|</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>𝐛</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>𝐛</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>𝜹</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>𝐛</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>𝐛</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>𝜹</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></mfrac><mo>|</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{1}=|\hat{\mathbf{a}}\cdot\mathbf{b}|\,\left|\frac{\|\mathbf{b}\|_{2}-\|\mathbf{b}+\bm{\delta}\|_{2}}{\|\mathbf{b}\|_{2}\,\|\mathbf{b}+\bm{\delta}\|_{2}}\right|</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A4.Thmlemma2.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.Thmlemma2.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.Thmlemma2.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text">Using Cauchy–Schwarz (<math id="A4.Thmlemma2.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|\hat{\mathbf{a}}\cdot\mathbf{b}|\leq\|\mathbf{b}\|_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐚</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mi>𝐛</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>𝐛</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|\hat{\mathbf{a}}\cdot\mathbf{b}|\leq\|\mathbf{b}\|_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>), and the reverse triangle inequality (<math id="A4.Thmlemma2.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bigl|\|\mathbf{b}\|_{2}-\|\mathbf{b}+\bm{\delta}\|_{2}\bigr|\leq\|\bm{\delta}\|_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em" stretchy="true">|</mo><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>𝐛</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>𝐛</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>𝜹</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em" stretchy="true">|</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>𝜹</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bigl|\|\mathbf{b}\|_{2}-\|\mathbf{b}+\bm{\delta}\|_{2}\bigr|\leq\|\bm{\delta}\|_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>) again, we get:
<math id="A4.Thmlemma2.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{1}\leq\|\mathbf{b}\|_{2}\,\frac{\|\bm{\delta}\|_{2}}{\|\mathbf{b}\|_{2}(\|\mathbf{b}\|_{2}-\|\bm{\delta}\|_{2})}=\frac{\|\bm{\delta}\|_{2}}{\|\mathbf{b}\|_{2}-\|\bm{\delta}\|_{2}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>T</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>≤</mo><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>𝐛</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mfrac><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>𝜹</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>𝐛</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>𝐛</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>𝜹</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>𝜹</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>𝐛</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>𝜹</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{1}\leq\|\mathbf{b}\|_{2}\,\frac{\|\bm{\delta}\|_{2}}{\|\mathbf{b}\|_{2}(\|\mathbf{b}\|_{2}-\|\bm{\delta}\|_{2})}=\frac{\|\bm{\delta}\|_{2}}{\|\mathbf{b}\|_{2}-\|\bm{\delta}\|_{2}}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Summing <math id="A4.Thmlemma2.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>T</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A4.Thmlemma2.p5.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>T</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> completes the proof.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A4.Thmlemma2.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.Thmlemma2.p6.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.Thmlemma2.p6.1.1" class="ltx_text">∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.1 </span>Main Result: Achievable PCC Gain</h3>

<div id="A4.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We now combine these lemmas to prove the main theorem regarding the capacity ceiling of convex attention.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.Thmtheorem1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_theorem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A4.Thmtheorem1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem D.1</span></span><span id="A4.Thmtheorem1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Achievable PCC Gain Bound for Convex Attention)<span id="A4.Thmtheorem1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="A4.Thmtheorem1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.Thmtheorem1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.Thmtheorem1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="A4.Thmtheorem1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> be the PCC achieved by the mean-pooling baseline <math id="A4.Thmtheorem1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{\mathbf{y}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐲</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{\mathbf{y}}</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A4.Thmtheorem1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ρ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho</annotation></semantics></math> the PCC achieved by any convex attention mechanism <math id="A4.Thmtheorem1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\mathbf{y}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐲</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\mathbf{y}}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Assume <math id="A4.Thmtheorem1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|\mathbf{w}\|_{2}&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>𝐰</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\mathbf{w}\|_{2}&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>. If the intrinsic dispersion is small relative to the baseline variation such that <math id="A4.Thmtheorem1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{R}&lt;\sigma_{0}/\|\mathbf{w}\|_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>R</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo>&lt;</mo><mrow><msub><mi>σ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>/</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>𝐰</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{R}&lt;\sigma_{0}/\|\mathbf{w}\|_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, then:</span></p>
<table id="A4.Ex16" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.Ex16.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|\rho-\rho_{0}|\;\leq\;\frac{2\,\|\mathbf{w}\|_{2}\,\tilde{R}}{\sigma_{0}-\|\mathbf{w}\|_{2}\,\tilde{R}}\;=\;\frac{2\,\tilde{R}}{\sigma_{0}/\|\mathbf{w}\|_{2}-\tilde{R}}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow><mo rspace="0.280em" stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.558em">≤</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>𝐰</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>R</mi><mo>~</mo></mover></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>σ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>𝐰</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>R</mi><mo>~</mo></mover></mrow></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0.558em" rspace="0.558em">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>R</mi><mo>~</mo></mover></mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>σ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>/</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>𝐰</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo>−</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>R</mi><mo>~</mo></mover></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|\rho-\rho_{0}|\;\leq\;\frac{2\,\|\mathbf{w}\|_{2}\,\tilde{R}}{\sigma_{0}-\|\mathbf{w}\|_{2}\,\tilde{R}}\;=\;\frac{2\,\tilde{R}}{\sigma_{0}/\|\mathbf{w}\|_{2}-\tilde{R}}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS1.2" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A4.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.SS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text">We apply <a href="#A4.Thmlemma2" title="Lemma D.2 (Correlation perturbation). ‣ General Correlation Perturbation Lemma. ‣ Appendix D Achievable PCC Bound of Convex Attention Models ‣ Breaking the Correlation Plateau: On the Optimization and Capacity Limits of Attention-Based Regressors" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Lemma</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">D.2</span></a> using the centered vectors: <math id="A4.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{m}=\mathbf{a}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐦</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>𝐚</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{m}=\mathbf{a}</annotation></semantics></math> (centered targets), <math id="A4.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{n}=\bar{\mathbf{b}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐧</mi><mo>=</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐛</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{n}=\bar{\mathbf{b}}</annotation></semantics></math> (centered baseline predictions), and <math id="A4.SS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{\delta}=\Delta\mathbf{b}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝜹</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐛</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{\delta}=\Delta\mathbf{b}</annotation></semantics></math> (centered attention perturbation).</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.SS1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text">First, we relate the L2 norms of the centered vectors to the defined dispersion measures. By the definition of the empirical standard deviation <math id="A4.SS1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>σ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{0}</annotation></semantics></math>, we have:</span></p>
<table id="A4.Ex17" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.Ex17.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|\bar{\mathbf{b}}\|_{2}=\sqrt{\sum_{s}(\bar{y}_{s}-\mu_{\bar{y}})^{2}}=\sqrt{S}\,\sigma_{0}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐛</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mi>s</mi></munder><msup><mrow><mo lspace="0em" stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>μ</mi><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mrow><msqrt><mi>S</mi></msqrt><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>σ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\bar{\mathbf{b}}\|_{2}=\sqrt{\sum_{s}(\bar{y}_{s}-\mu_{\bar{y}})^{2}}=\sqrt{S}\,\sigma_{0}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS1.p3.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.SS1.p3.2.1" class="ltx_text">By <a href="#A4.Thmlemma1" title="Lemma D.1 (Bound on Prediction Perturbation). ‣ Bounding the Attention Perturbation. ‣ Appendix D Achievable PCC Bound of Convex Attention Models ‣ Breaking the Correlation Plateau: On the Optimization and Capacity Limits of Attention-Based Regressors" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Lemma</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">D.1</span></a>, the perturbation is bounded by:</span></p>
<table id="A4.Ex18" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.Ex18.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|\Delta\mathbf{b}\|_{2}\leq\sqrt{S}\,\|\mathbf{w}\|_{2}\,\tilde{R}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐛</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>≤</mo><mrow><msqrt><mi>S</mi></msqrt><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>𝐰</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>R</mi><mo>~</mo></mover></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\Delta\mathbf{b}\|_{2}\leq\sqrt{S}\,\|\mathbf{w}\|_{2}\,\tilde{R}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS1.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.SS1.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text">Next, we verify the condition required for <a href="#A4.Thmlemma2" title="Lemma D.2 (Correlation perturbation). ‣ General Correlation Perturbation Lemma. ‣ Appendix D Achievable PCC Bound of Convex Attention Models ‣ Breaking the Correlation Plateau: On the Optimization and Capacity Limits of Attention-Based Regressors" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Lemma</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">D.2</span></a>, <math id="A4.SS1.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|\bm{\delta}\|_{2}&lt;\|\mathbf{n}\|_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>𝜹</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>&lt;</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>𝐧</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\bm{\delta}\|_{2}&lt;\|\mathbf{n}\|_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.
The assumption <math id="A4.SS1.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{R}&lt;\sigma_{0}/\|\mathbf{w}\|_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>R</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo>&lt;</mo><mrow><msub><mi>σ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>/</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>𝐰</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{R}&lt;\sigma_{0}/\|\mathbf{w}\|_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> implies <math id="A4.SS1.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|\mathbf{w}\|_{2}\,\tilde{R}&lt;\sigma_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>𝐰</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>R</mi><mo>~</mo></mover></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><msub><mi>σ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\mathbf{w}\|_{2}\,\tilde{R}&lt;\sigma_{0}</annotation></semantics></math>. Multiplying by <math id="A4.SS1.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sqrt{S}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msqrt><mi>S</mi></msqrt><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{S}</annotation></semantics></math>, we get:</span></p>
<table id="A4.Ex19" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.Ex19.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sqrt{S}\,\|\mathbf{w}\|_{2}\,\tilde{R}&lt;\sqrt{S}\,\sigma_{0}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msqrt><mi>S</mi></msqrt><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>𝐰</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>R</mi><mo>~</mo></mover></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mrow><msqrt><mi>S</mi></msqrt><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>σ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{S}\,\|\mathbf{w}\|_{2}\,\tilde{R}&lt;\sqrt{S}\,\sigma_{0}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS1.p4.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.SS1.p4.2.1" class="ltx_text">Therefore, <math id="A4.SS1.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|\Delta\mathbf{b}\|_{2}&lt;\|\bar{\mathbf{b}}\|_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐛</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>&lt;</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐛</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\Delta\mathbf{b}\|_{2}&lt;\|\bar{\mathbf{b}}\|_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, satisfying the prerequisite.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS1.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS1.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.SS1.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text">Now, applying <a href="#A4.Thmlemma2" title="Lemma D.2 (Correlation perturbation). ‣ General Correlation Perturbation Lemma. ‣ Appendix D Achievable PCC Bound of Convex Attention Models ‣ Breaking the Correlation Plateau: On the Optimization and Capacity Limits of Attention-Based Regressors" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Lemma</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">D.2</span></a>:</span></p>
<table id="A4.Ex20" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.Ex20.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|\rho-\rho_{0}|\;\leq\;\frac{2\,\|\Delta\mathbf{b}\|_{2}}{\|\bar{\mathbf{b}}\|_{2}-\|\Delta\mathbf{b}\|_{2}}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow><mo rspace="0.280em" stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.558em">≤</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐛</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐛</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐛</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|\rho-\rho_{0}|\;\leq\;\frac{2\,\|\Delta\mathbf{b}\|_{2}}{\|\bar{\mathbf{b}}\|_{2}-\|\Delta\mathbf{b}\|_{2}}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS1.p5.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.SS1.p5.2.1" class="ltx_text">Since the function <math id="A4.SS1.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f(x)=2x/(C-x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo>/</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(x)=2x/(C-x)</annotation></semantics></math> is monotonically increasing for <math id="A4.SS1.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x&lt;C" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x&lt;C</annotation></semantics></math> (where <math id="A4.SS1.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C=\|\bar{\mathbf{b}}\|_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐛</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C=\|\bar{\mathbf{b}}\|_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>), we substitute the upper bound for <math id="A4.SS1.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|\Delta\mathbf{b}\|_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐛</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\Delta\mathbf{b}\|_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>:</span></p>
<table id="A4.EGx50" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A4.Ex21.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\;\leq\;\frac{2\,(\sqrt{S}\,\|\mathbf{w}\|_{2}\,\tilde{R})}{\sqrt{S}\,\sigma_{0}-(\sqrt{S}\,\|\mathbf{w}\|_{2}\,\tilde{R})}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo lspace="0.558em" rspace="0.558em">≤</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msqrt><mi>S</mi></msqrt><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>𝐰</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>R</mi><mo>~</mo></mover></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mrow><msqrt><mi>S</mi></msqrt><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>σ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msqrt><mi>S</mi></msqrt><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>𝐰</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>R</mi><mo>~</mo></mover></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mstyle></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\;\leq\;\frac{2\,(\sqrt{S}\,\|\mathbf{w}\|_{2}\,\tilde{R})}{\sqrt{S}\,\sigma_{0}-(\sqrt{S}\,\|\mathbf{w}\|_{2}\,\tilde{R})}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
<tbody id="A4.Ex22"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_eqn_cell"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A4.Ex22.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\;=\;\frac{2\,\|\mathbf{w}\|_{2}\,\tilde{R}}{\sigma_{0}-\|\mathbf{w}\|_{2}\,\tilde{R}}." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo lspace="0.558em" rspace="0.558em">=</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>𝐰</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>R</mi><mo>~</mo></mover></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>σ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>𝐰</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>R</mi><mo>~</mo></mover></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mstyle></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\;=\;\frac{2\,\|\mathbf{w}\|_{2}\,\tilde{R}}{\sigma_{0}-\|\mathbf{w}\|_{2}\,\tilde{R}}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS1.p5.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.SS1.p5.3.1" class="ltx_text">Dividing the numerator and denominator by <math id="A4.SS1.p5.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|\mathbf{w}\|_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>𝐰</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\mathbf{w}\|_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> (which is positive by assumption) yields the scale-invariant form:</span></p>
<table id="A4.Ex23" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.Ex23.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|\rho-\rho_{0}|\;\leq\;\frac{2\,\tilde{R}}{\sigma_{0}/\|\mathbf{w}\|_{2}-\tilde{R}}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow><mo rspace="0.280em" stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.558em">≤</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>R</mi><mo>~</mo></mover></mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>σ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>/</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>𝐰</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo>−</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>R</mi><mo>~</mo></mover></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|\rho-\rho_{0}|\;\leq\;\frac{2\,\tilde{R}}{\sigma_{0}/\|\mathbf{w}\|_{2}-\tilde{R}}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS1.p5.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.SS1.p5.4.1" class="ltx_text">∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.2 </span>Connection between In-sample Dispersion and Radius</h3>

<div id="A4.Thmlemma3" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lemma">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A4.Thmlemma3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma D.3</span></span><span id="A4.Thmlemma3.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Dispersion–Radius Connection)<span id="A4.Thmlemma3.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="A4.Thmlemma3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.Thmlemma3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.Thmlemma3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For each sample <math id="A4.Thmlemma3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A4.Thmlemma3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{s}/\sqrt{n_{s}}\leq\sigma_{s}\leq R_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>/</mo><msqrt><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></msqrt></mrow><mo>≤</mo><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>≤</mo><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{s}/\sqrt{n_{s}}\leq\sigma_{s}\leq R_{s}</annotation></semantics></math>. Consequently, we denote <math id="A4.Thmlemma3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{\sigma}:=\Bigl(\frac{1}{S}\sum_{s=1}^{S}\sigma_{s}^{2}\Bigr)^{1/2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>σ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo>:=</mo><msup><mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">(</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>S</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>S</mi></msubsup><msubsup><mi>σ</mi><mi>s</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{\sigma}:=\Bigl(\frac{1}{S}\sum_{s=1}^{S}\sigma_{s}^{2}\Bigr)^{1/2}</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="A4.Thmlemma3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n_{\max}=\max_{s}n_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>max</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>max</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n_{\max}=\max_{s}n_{s}</annotation></semantics></math>, we have
<math id="A4.Thmlemma3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{R}/\sqrt{n_{\max}}\leq\tilde{\sigma}\leq\tilde{R}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>R</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo>/</mo><msqrt><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>max</mi></msub></msqrt></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>σ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo>≤</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>R</mi><mo>~</mo></mover></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{R}/\sqrt{n_{\max}}\leq\tilde{\sigma}\leq\tilde{R}</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A5" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix E </span>Generality of Theoretical Analysis Regarding Architecture Depth</h2>

<div id="A5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">A potential concern regarding our theoretical analysis is whether the findings derived for attention aggregation apply to deep, multi-layer architectures. In this section, we clarify that our analysis focuses on the aggregation mechanism at the readout stage, which dictates the final prediction behavior regardless of the depth of the preceding backbone.</p>
</div>
<div id="A5.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Backbone-Agnostic Formulation.</span> Our theoretical model assumes input embeddings <math id="A5.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{h}_{s}=\{\mathbf{h}_{si}\}_{i=1}^{n_{s}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐡</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>𝐡</mi><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{h}_{s}=\{\mathbf{h}_{si}\}_{i=1}^{n_{s}}</annotation></semantics></math>. In the context of deep learning, these are not raw inputs but rather the latent representations produced by a backbone function <math id="A5.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{\theta}(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{\theta}(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math> (comprising multiple Transformer blocks, FFNs, residual connections, and LayerNorms). The final prediction is modeled as <math id="A5.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{y}_{s}=\mathbf{w}^{\top}\mathbf{v}_{s}+c" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>𝐰</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐯</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{y}_{s}=\mathbf{w}^{\top}\mathbf{v}_{s}+c</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="A5.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{v}_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐯</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{v}_{s}</annotation></semantics></math> is a convex combination of these final-layer representations. This formulation exactly matches the standard architectural paradigm used in modern Transformers:</p>
<ul id="A5.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="A5.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A5.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">[CLS] Token Aggregation:</span> In models like BERT or ViT, the prediction is often derived from a specific [CLS] token. However, in a standard Transformer layer, the output embedding of the [CLS] token is computed via the attention mechanism, which is a convex combination (softmax) of the element embeddings from the previous layer. Thus, the readout remains a convex aggregation of the backbone’s features, subject to the analysis we present.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A5.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A5.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Global Average Pooling:</span> Many regression heads utilize global average pooling over token embeddings, which is a special case of convex attention where uniform weights are applied (<math id="A5.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha_{si}=1/n_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>α</mi><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha_{si}=1/n_{s}</annotation></semantics></math>).</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
<div id="A5.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">The Readout Bottleneck.</span> Our analysis (<a href="#S2.Thmtheorem2" title="Theorem 2.2 (PCC Gain Bound for Convex Attention). ‣ Prediction Decompositon. ‣ 2.4 Model Capacity: The PCC Ceiling of Convex Aggregation ‣ 2 Theoretical Analysis of Correlation Learning in Attention-based Aggregation ‣ Breaking the Correlation Plateau: On the Optimization and Capacity Limits of Attention-Based Regressors" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Theorem</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.2</span></a>) establishes that the achievable PCC gain is bounded by the convex hull of the input embeddings. Even with a highly expressive deep backbone <math id="A5.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math>, if the final aggregation step is convex, the prediction <math id="A5.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{y}_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{y}_{s}</annotation></semantics></math> is geometrically constrained to the interior of the simplex formed by the final-layer features <math id="A5.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{\mathbf{h}_{si}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>𝐡</mi><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{\mathbf{h}_{si}\}</annotation></semantics></math>. Crucially, deep backbones do not inherently solve the <em id="A5.p3.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">homogeneity</em> issue. In fact, models pre-trained with contrastive objectives often produce highly homogeneous embeddings for in-sample elements (semantically similar tokens or patches), which shrinks the convex hull radius <math id="A5.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{s}</annotation></semantics></math> and exacerbates the capacity limitation.</p>
</div>
<div id="A5.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Empirical Validation on Deep Architectures.</span> Our experimental evaluation in <a href="#S5.T1" title="In 5.1 Experimental Setup ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ Breaking the Correlation Plateau: On the Optimization and Capacity Limits of Attention-Based Regressors" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> and <a href="#S5.T2" title="In 5.2 Results and analysis ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ Breaking the Correlation Plateau: On the Optimization and Capacity Limits of Attention-Based Regressors" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> utilizes deep, multi-layer architectures, not shallow regressors.</p>
<ul id="A5.I2" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="A5.I2.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A5.I2.i1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.I2.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.I2.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">FT-Transformer:</span> A deep tabular Transformer with multiple attention layers.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A5.I2.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A5.I2.i2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.I2.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.I2.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">ALMT:</span> A complex multimodal Transformer for sentiment analysis.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A5.I2.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A5.I2.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.I2.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.I2.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">EGN:</span> A multi-layer vision Transformer model for spatial transcriptomics.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
<p id="A5.p4.2" class="ltx_p">In all these deep settings, we observed the PCC plateau phenomenon. The consistent improvement provided by ECA confirms that the convex readout mechanism acts as a bottleneck even in deep models, and that relaxing this constraint via extrapolative mechanisms is necessary for optimal correlation learning.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A6" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix F </span>Extended Empirical Evidence of the PCC Plateau</h2>

<div id="A6.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To rigorously address the universality of the PCC plateau phenomenon and demonstrate that it is not an artifact of specific datasets or architectures, we conducted extensive additional experiments on 8 diverse regression benchmarks from the UCI Machine Learning Repository <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib41" title="" class="ltx_ref">Asuncion et al., 2007</a>)</cite>. We utilized a multi-layer FT-Transformer <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gorishniy et al., 2021</a>)</cite> as the backbone to represent modern, high-capacity attention-based regression models.</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A6.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><a href="#A6.F7" title="In Appendix F Extended Empirical Evidence of the PCC Plateau ‣ Breaking the Correlation Plateau: On the Optimization and Capacity Limits of Attention-Based Regressors" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a> illustrates the training (left) and validation (right) trajectories for both MSE and PCC. The curves marked with circles represent PCC metric, while the curves without circle represent MSE.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A6.F7" class="ltx_figure ltx_align_center">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 7: </span>Training and validation curves for multi-layer FT-Transformer on 8 UCI regression datasets. <span id="A6.F7.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Left:</span> Training set metrics. <span id="A6.F7.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Right:</span> Validation set metrics. The curves with <span id="A6.F7.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">circles</span> indicate PCC (maximizing shape matching), while curves <span id="A6.F7.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">without circles</span> indicate MSE (minimizing magnitude error). In all instances, PCC hits a ceiling (plateau) significantly earlier than MSE, which continues to descend, highlighting the optimization gap.</figcaption>
</figure>

<div id="A6.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A6.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Observations and Analysis:</span></p>
<ul id="A6.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="A6.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A6.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A6.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Decoupling of MSE and PCC:</span> Across all 8 datasets, we observe a distinct decoupling of the two metrics. In the early stages of training, both MSE and PCC improve. However, a distinct inflection point: the “PCC Plateau” consistently appears where the correlation gain flattens.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A6.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A6.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A6.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Persistent MSE Reduction:</span> Crucially, after the PCC plateaus, the MSE continues to decrease significantly. This confirms the optimization conflict identified in our theoretical analysis (<a href="#S2.Thmremark3" title="Remark 2.3 (The Two Bottlenecks of Softmax Attention for Correlation). ‣ Gradient Decomposition and the Optimization Conflict. ‣ 2.3 Optimization Dynamics: The Correlation Gradient Bottleneck ‣ 2 Theoretical Analysis of Correlation Learning in Attention-based Aggregation ‣ Breaking the Correlation Plateau: On the Optimization and Capacity Limits of Attention-Based Regressors" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Remark</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.3</span></a>): the gradient dynamics of MSE minimization (specifically standard deviation matching) actively suppress the correlation gradient magnitude. The model continues to learn magnitude information (lowering MSE) but loses the ability to optimize the shape/ordering of predictions (PCC).</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A6.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A6.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Universality:</span> Despite varying noise levels and feature dimensions across these diverse real-world datasets, the optimization pattern in correlation learning remains identical. This provides robust empirical evidence that the PCC plateau is a fundamental failure mode in joint MSE-PCC training with attention-based models, which calls for a specific architectural improvement as we proposed in <a href="#S3" title="3 Extrapolative Correlation Attention (ECA) ‣ Breaking the Correlation Plateau: On the Optimization and Capacity Limits of Attention-Based Regressors" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A7" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix G </span>Detailed Experimental Settings</h2>

<section id="A7.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">G.1 </span>Synthetic Experiment Details</h3>

<section id="A7.SS1.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">G.1.1 </span>Detailed Data Generation Process</h4>

<div id="A7.SS1.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS1.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We provide a detailed description of the synthetic dataset generation process (DGP). The DGP is parameterized by the embedding dimension <math id="A7.SS1.SSS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>D</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D</annotation></semantics></math>, the number of elements per sample <math id="A7.SS1.SSS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math>, the signal contrast <math id="A7.SS1.SSS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>η</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta</annotation></semantics></math>, the noise level <math id="A7.SS1.SSS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nu" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ν</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nu</annotation></semantics></math>, the ground truth extrapolation factor <math id="A7.SS1.SSS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma^{*}\geq 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>γ</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma^{*}\geq 1</annotation></semantics></math>, the cross-sample variation scale <math id="A7.SS1.SSS1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{B}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>B</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{B}</annotation></semantics></math>, and a noise floor <math id="A7.SS1.SSS1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{\text{floor}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>σ</mi><mtext>floor</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{\text{floor}}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<section id="A7.SS1.SSS1.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">1. Defining Ground Truth Directions.</h5>

<div id="A7.SS1.SSS1.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS1.SSS1.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We first establish the direction of the signal and the direction of the noise.</p>
<ol id="A7.I1" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="A7.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="A7.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Sample the ground truth regression vector (signal direction) <math id="A7.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{w}^{*}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\mathbf{I}_{D})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>𝐰</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝐈</mi><mi>D</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{w}^{*}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\mathbf{I}_{D})</annotation></semantics></math>. Normalize <math id="A7.I1.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|\mathbf{w}^{*}\|_{2}=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><msup><mi>𝐰</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\mathbf{w}^{*}\|_{2}=1</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A7.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="A7.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Sample a noise direction vector <math id="A7.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{w}^{\perp}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>𝐰</mi><mo>⟂</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{w}^{\perp}</annotation></semantics></math>. We ensure orthogonality (<math id="A7.I1.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\mathbf{w}^{*})^{\top}\mathbf{w}^{\perp}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>𝐰</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>𝐰</mi><mo>⟂</mo></msup></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\mathbf{w}^{*})^{\top}\mathbf{w}^{\perp}=0</annotation></semantics></math>) using the Gram-Schmidt process and normalize <math id="A7.I1.i2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|\mathbf{w}^{\perp}\|_{2}=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><msup><mi>𝐰</mi><mo>⟂</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\mathbf{w}^{\perp}\|_{2}=1</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div></li>
</ol>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A7.SS1.SSS1.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">2. Generating Sample Centers.</h5>

<div id="A7.SS1.SSS1.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS1.SSS1.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For each sample <math id="A7.SS1.SSS1.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s\in\{1,\dots,S\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>S</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s\in\{1,\dots,S\}</annotation></semantics></math>, we sample the sample center (mean embedding) from an isotropic Gaussian distribution, controlling the cross-sample variation:</p>

<section id="A7.SS1.SSS1.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">3. Generating Elements.</h5>

<div id="A7.SS1.SSS1.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS1.SSS1.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We generate <math id="A7.SS1.SSS1.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> elements for each sample <math id="A7.SS1.SSS1.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math>, distinguishing between <math id="A7.SS1.SSS1.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K-1</annotation></semantics></math> background samples and one key sample.</p>
</div>
<div id="A7.SS1.SSS1.Px3.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS1.SSS1.Px3.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A7.SS1.SSS1.Px3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Background Elements</span> (<math id="A7.SS1.SSS1.Px3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i=1,\dots,K-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i=1,\dots,K-1</annotation></semantics></math>): These elements are generated by adding small isotropic noise (noise floor) to the sample center:</p>
<table id="A7.E97" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<p id="A7.SS1.SSS1.Px3.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A7.SS1.SSS1.Px3.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Key Element</span> (<math id="A7.SS1.SSS1.Px3.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i=K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i=K</annotation></semantics></math>): The key element is generated by explicitly injecting signal contrast along <math id="A7.SS1.SSS1.Px3.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{w}^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>𝐰</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{w}^{*}</annotation></semantics></math> and uninformative noise along <math id="A7.SS1.SSS1.Px3.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{w}^{\perp}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>𝐰</mi><mo>⟂</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{w}^{\perp}</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>

</section>
<section id="A7.SS1.SSS1.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">4. Defining the Target Variable.</h5>

<div id="A7.SS1.SSS1.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS1.SSS1.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The target variable is defined based on an optimal representation <math id="A7.SS1.SSS1.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{v}_{s}^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>𝐯</mi><mi>s</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{v}_{s}^{*}</annotation></semantics></math> that extrapolates the <em id="A7.SS1.SSS1.Px4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">signal component</em> by the factor <math id="A7.SS1.SSS1.Px4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>γ</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma^{*}</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="A7.E99" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A7.E99.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{v}_{s}^{*}=\bm{\mu}_{s}+\gamma^{*}\cdot(\eta\cdot\mathbf{w}^{*})." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>𝐯</mi><mi>s</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝝁</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><msup><mi>γ</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msup><mi>𝐰</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{v}_{s}^{*}=\bm{\mu}_{s}+\gamma^{*}\cdot(\eta\cdot\mathbf{w}^{*}).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(99)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A7.SS1.SSS1.Px4.p1.2" class="ltx_p">The target label <math id="A7.SS1.SSS1.Px4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y_{s}</annotation></semantics></math> is generated by applying the ground truth regression vector <math id="A7.SS1.SSS1.Px4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{w}^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>𝐰</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{w}^{*}</annotation></semantics></math> to this optimal representation, with added label noise <math id="A7.SS1.SSS1.Px4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon^{\prime}_{s}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\sigma_{\text{label}}^{2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>ϵ</mi><mi>s</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>σ</mi><mtext>label</mtext><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon^{\prime}_{s}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\sigma_{\text{label}}^{2})</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="A7.E100" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A7.E100.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y_{s}=(\mathbf{w}^{*})^{\top}\mathbf{v}_{s}^{*}+\epsilon^{\prime}_{s}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>𝐰</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐯</mi><mi>s</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup></mrow><mo>+</mo><msubsup><mi>ϵ</mi><mi>s</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y_{s}=(\mathbf{w}^{*})^{\top}\mathbf{v}_{s}^{*}+\epsilon^{\prime}_{s}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(100)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A7.SS1.SSS2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">G.1.2 </span>Experimental Setup and Hyperparameters</h4>

<section id="A7.SS1.SSS2.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Model Architecture.</h5>

<div id="A7.SS1.SSS2.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS1.SSS2.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We use a simple gating attention architecture. The element embeddings <math id="A7.SS1.SSS2.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{h}_{si}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐡</mi><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{h}_{si}</annotation></semantics></math> are generated directly by the DGP (no pre-trained encoder). The attention logits are computed via a linear layer parameterized by <math id="A7.SS1.SSS2.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{w}_{\text{attn}}\in\mathbb{R}^{D\times 1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐰</mi><mtext>attn</mtext></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{w}_{\text{attn}}\in\mathbb{R}^{D\times 1}</annotation></semantics></math>: <math id="A7.SS1.SSS2.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{si}=\mathbf{h}_{si}^{\top}\mathbf{w}_{\text{attn}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>𝐡</mi><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐰</mi><mtext>attn</mtext></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{si}=\mathbf{h}_{si}^{\top}\mathbf{w}_{\text{attn}}</annotation></semantics></math>. The aggregated sample-level representation <math id="A7.SS1.SSS2.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{v}_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐯</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{v}_{s}</annotation></semantics></math> is computed using <math id="A7.SS1.SSS2.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{v}_{s}=\sum_{i=1}^{n_{s}}\operatorname{Softmax}(\{z_{si}\}_{i=1}^{n_{s}})\mathbf{h}_{si}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐯</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></msubsup><mrow><mrow><mi>Softmax</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐡</mi><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{v}_{s}=\sum_{i=1}^{n_{s}}\operatorname{Softmax}(\{z_{si}\}_{i=1}^{n_{s}})\mathbf{h}_{si}</annotation></semantics></math>. The final prediction is computed via a regression head <math id="A7.SS1.SSS2.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}_{\text{reg}}\in\mathbb{R}^{D\times 1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mtext>reg</mtext></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}_{\text{reg}}\in\mathbb{R}^{D\times 1}</annotation></semantics></math> and bias <math id="A7.SS1.SSS2.Px1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>b</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b</annotation></semantics></math>: <math id="A7.SS1.SSS2.Px1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{y}_{s}=\mathbf{v}_{s}^{\top}\mathbf{w}+b" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>𝐯</mi><mi>s</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐰</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{y}_{s}=\mathbf{v}_{s}^{\top}\mathbf{w}+b</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A7.SS1.SSS2.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Optimization.</h5>

<div id="A7.SS1.SSS2.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS1.SSS2.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We train the models using the Adam optimizer <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib46" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kingma, 2014</a>)</cite> with standard parameters (<math id="A7.SS1.SSS2.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta_{1}=0.9,\beta_{2}=0.999,\epsilon=10^{-8}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>β</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.9</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>β</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.999</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>ϵ</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta_{1}=0.9,\beta_{2}=0.999,\epsilon=10^{-8}</annotation></semantics></math>). The objective function is the joint loss <math id="A7.SS1.SSS2.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\text{total}}=\mathcal{L}_{\text{MSE}}+\lambda_{\text{PCC}}\mathcal{L}_{\text{PCC}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>total</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>MSE</mtext></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mtext>PCC</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>PCC</mtext></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\text{total}}=\mathcal{L}_{\text{MSE}}+\lambda_{\text{PCC}}\mathcal{L}_{\text{PCC}}</annotation></semantics></math> (or <math id="A7.SS1.SSS2.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{\mathcal{L}}_{\text{PCC}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mtext>PCC</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{\mathcal{L}}_{\text{PCC}}</annotation></semantics></math> in <a href="#S3.E11" title="In 3.3 Stabilizing Optimization: Dispersion-Normalized PCC Loss (DNPL) ‣ 3 Extrapolative Correlation Attention (ECA) ‣ Breaking the Correlation Plateau: On the Optimization and Capacity Limits of Attention-Based Regressors" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Equation</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">11</span></a> for DNPL).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A7.SS1.SSS2.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
