<section id="A7.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">G.2 </span>UCI ML Repository Datasets</h3>

<div id="A7.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For each dataset, We report PCC, MSE and MAE between predictions <math id="A7.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{y}_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{y}_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> and ground-truth targets <math id="A7.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> over all samples in test set is</p>
<table id="A7.Ex24" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A7.Ex24.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{PCC}\left(\hat{y},y\right)=\frac{\operatorname{cov}\!\left(\hat{y},y\right)}{\sigma(\hat{y})\,\sigma(y)}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>PCC</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mpadded style="width:1.268em;" width="1.268em"><mi>cov</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{PCC}\left(\hat{y},y\right)=\frac{\operatorname{cov}\!\left(\hat{y},y\right)}{\sigma(\hat{y})\,\sigma(y)}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A7.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Mean squared error (MSE) and mean absolute error (MAE) are computed sample-wise and averaged over all gene–window pairs:</p>
<table id="A7.Ex25" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A7.Ex25.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{MSE}\left(\hat{y},y\right)=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}(\hat{y}_{i}-y_{i})^{2},\qquad\mathrm{MAE}\left(\hat{y},y\right)=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}\lvert\hat{y}_{i}-y_{i}\rvert." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>MSE</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>N</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false" rspace="0em">∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></munderover><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>MAE</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>N</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false" rspace="0em">∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></munderover><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{MSE}\left(\hat{y},y\right)=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}(\hat{y}_{i}-y_{i})^{2},\qquad\mathrm{MAE}\left(\hat{y},y\right)=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}\lvert\hat{y}_{i}-y_{i}\rvert.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<section id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">1. Appliance Dataset</h5>

<div id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The Appliances Energy Prediction dataset from the UCI Machine Learning Repository contains experimental data collected over 4.5 months in a low-energy building. It includes 19,735 instances with 28 real-valued features, including indoor temperature, humidity, and weather conditions. These attributes are recorded at 10-minute intervals. The goal is to predict appliance energy usage as an integer value in watt-hours (Wh).</p>
</div>
<div id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We replace the attention layer in the FT-Transformer <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gorishniy et al., 2021</a>)</cite> with our ECA module and keep the remaining components unchanged. We use the following hyperparameters during training: “batch_size=128”, “dropout_rate=0.1”, “embedding_dim=256” and “num_heads=8” for both the FT-Transformer baseline and the FT-Transformer+ECA model. We use MSE and MAE to evaluate magnitude matching and PCC to evaluate correlation matching.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">2. Online News Dataset</h5>

<div id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The Online News Popularity dataset contains 39,797 news articles from Mashable, each described by 58 numeric features (with the URL and timedelta features excluded). Its target is the article’s number of social-media shares (popularity) and we applied the log transformation on the target to reduce the large range of data.</p>
</div>
<div id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We replace the attention layer in the FT-Transformer <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gorishniy et al., 2021</a>)</cite> with our ECA module and keep the remaining components unchanged. We use the following hyperparameters during training: “batch_size=128”, “dropout_rate=0.1”, “embedding_dim=256” and “num_heads=8” for both the FT-Transformer baseline and the FT-Transformer+ECA model. We use MSE and MAE to evaluate magnitude matching and PCC to evaluate correlation matching.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">3. Superconductivity Dataset</h5>

<div id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The UCI Superconductivity dataset contains 21,263 superconductors with 81 real-valued features, where the target is the critical temperature.</p>
</div>
<div id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We replace the attention layer in the FT-Transformer <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gorishniy et al., 2021</a>)</cite> with our ECA module and keep the remaining components unchanged. We use the following hyperparameters during training: “batch_size=128”, “dropout_rate=0.1”, “embedding_dim=256” and “num_heads=8” for both the FT-Transformer baseline and the FT-Transformer+ECA model. We use MSE and MAE to evaluate magnitude matching and PCC to evaluate correlation matching.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A7.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">G.3 </span>Spatial Transcriptomic Dataset</h3>

<section id="A7.SS3.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Data Processing.</h5>

<div id="A7.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We follow the data processing as the EGN baseline <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yang et al., 2023</a>)</cite>. The 10xProteomic dataset contains <math id="A7.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sim" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>∼</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sim</annotation></semantics></math>32,032 image–patch/expression pairs curated from 5 whole-slide images <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib26" title="" class="ltx_ref">Genomics, 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yang et al., 2023</a>)</cite>. Prediction targets are restricted to the 250 genes with the largest mean expression across the dataset (computed over all patches). For each target gene, we apply a log transform to expression values and then perform per-gene min–max normalization to map values into <math id="A7.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[0,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0,1]</annotation></semantics></math>. We use the dataset-provided image patches without modifying tiling or slide-level grouping.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A7.SS3.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Evaluation Metric.</h5>

<div id="A7.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We report PCC aggregated across genes and sample-wise error metrics. For each gene <math id="A7.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math>, PCC between predictions <math id="A7.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{y}_{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>g</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{y}_{g}</annotation></semantics></math> and ground truths <math id="A7.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y_{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y_{g}</annotation></semantics></math> over all evaluation windows is</p>
<table id="A7.Ex26" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A7.Ex26.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{PCC}(g)=\frac{\operatorname{cov}\!\left(\hat{y}_{g},y_{g}\right)}{\sigma(\hat{y}_{g})\,\sigma(y_{g})}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>PCC</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mpadded style="width:1.268em;" width="1.268em"><mi>cov</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>g</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{PCC}(g)=\frac{\operatorname{cov}\!\left(\hat{y}_{g},y_{g}\right)}{\sigma(\hat{y}_{g})\,\sigma(y_{g})}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A7.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">We summarize <math id="A7.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{\mathrm{PCC}(g)\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mi>PCC</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{\mathrm{PCC}(g)\}</annotation></semantics></math> across all target genes using:
<math id="A7.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{PCC@F}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>PCC</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>@</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>F</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{PCC@F}</annotation></semantics></math> (25th percentile), <math id="A7.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{PCC@S}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>PCC</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>@</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>S</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{PCC@S}</annotation></semantics></math> (median), and <math id="A7.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{PCC@M}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>PCC</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>@</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{PCC@M}</annotation></semantics></math> (mean). Higher is better.</p>
</div>
<div id="A7.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Mean squared error (MSE) and mean absolute error (MAE) are computed sample-wise and averaged over all gene–window pairs:</p>
<table id="A7.Ex27" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A7.Ex27.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{MSE}=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}(\hat{y}_{i}-y_{i})^{2},\qquad\mathrm{MAE}=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}\lvert\hat{y}_{i}-y_{i}\rvert." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>MSE</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>N</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false" rspace="0em">∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></munderover><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><mi>MAE</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>N</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false" rspace="0em">∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></munderover><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{MSE}=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}(\hat{y}_{i}-y_{i})^{2},\qquad\mathrm{MAE}=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}\lvert\hat{y}_{i}-y_{i}\rvert.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A7.SS3.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Implementation.</h5>

<div id="A7.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The EGN and ECA improved version are implemented in PyTorch. The visual backbone is a ViT with patch size 32, embedding dimension 1024, MLP dimension 4096, 16 attention heads, and depth 8. We interleave the proposed Exemplar Block (EB) every two ViT blocks. Each EB uses 16 heads with head dimension 64, retrieving the <math id="A7.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k{=}9" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k{=}9</annotation></semantics></math> nearest exemplars. Results are reported on a three-fold cross-validation with the same experimental setting in EGN. We train for 50 epochs with a batch size of 32. Experiments run on 2<math id="A7.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math> A6000 GPUs. We apply the same preprocessing and gene-selection protocol throughout and keep dataset-provided tiles and slide/patient groupings intact for fair comparison.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A7.SS3.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Extra Results.</h5>

<div id="A7.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><a href="#A6.F8" title="In Extra Results. ‣ G.3 Spatial Transcriptomic Dataset ‣ Appendix G Detailed Experimental Settings ‣ Breaking the Correlation Plateau: On the Optimization and Capacity Limits of Attention-Based Regressors" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a> and  <a href="#A7.F9" title="In Extra Results. ‣ G.3 Spatial Transcriptomic Dataset ‣ Appendix G Detailed Experimental Settings ‣ Breaking the Correlation Plateau: On the Optimization and Capacity Limits of Attention-Based Regressors" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a> provide extra visualization results on PCC@S and PCC@F metrics for each fold.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A6.F8" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2602.17898v1/app_st_pccF.svg" id="A6.F8.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:548/114;" width="548" height="114"></object>

</section>
</section>
<section id="A7.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">G.4 </span>Multimodal Sentiment Analysis (MSA) Dataset</h3>

<section id="A7.SS4.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Data Processing</h5>

<div id="A7.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We conduct multimodal sentiment analysis (MSA) experiments on the CMU-MOSI dataset <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib30" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zadeh et al., 2016</a>)</cite>, a standard benchmark comprising <math id="A7.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\,2{,}199\," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn> 2,199</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\,2{,}199\,</annotation></semantics></math> opinion-centric video segments. Each segment pairs a short monologue clip with synchronized <em id="A7.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">language</em>, <em id="A7.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">acoustic</em>, and <em id="A7.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">visual</em> modalities and is annotated with a continuous sentiment intensity score on a seven-point scale from <math id="A7.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-3</annotation></semantics></math> (strongly negative) to <math id="A7.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+3</annotation></semantics></math> (strongly positive). Following the widely adopted split, the data are partitioned into <math id="A7.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\,1{,}284\,/\,229\,/\,686\," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn> 1,284</mn><mo lspace="0.392em">/</mo><mn> 229</mn><mo lspace="0.392em">/</mo><mn> 686</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\,1{,}284\,/\,229\,/\,686\,</annotation></semantics></math> segments for train/validation/test. In line with community practice and THUIAR’s public releases <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib29" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yu et al., 2020</a>; <a href="#bib.bib28" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yu et al., 2021</a>)</cite>, we use pre-extracted, unaligned features where acoustic streams are sampled at <math id="A7.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="12.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>12.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">12.5</annotation></semantics></math> Hz and visual streams at <math id="A7.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="15" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>15</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">15</annotation></semantics></math> Hz; text features are aligned to the same timeline.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A7.SS4.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Task formulation and metrics.</h5>

<div id="A7.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We evaluate models in the regression setting (predicting the continuous sentiment score) while also reporting the standard classification metric used in prior MSA work. Concretely, we report:
(i) MAE: mean absolute error between predicted and ground-truth sentiment;
(ii) PCC: Pearson’s correlation coefficient between predictions and ground truth, measuring rank/linear consistency; and
(iii) F1: the binary F1 score computed under the standard MOSI protocol from prior work and THUIAR’s toolkit <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib29" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yu et al., 2020</a>; <a href="#bib.bib28" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yu et al., 2021</a>)</cite>.
This suite jointly captures absolute deviation (MAE), correlation structure (PCC), and discrete decision quality (F1) and is consistent with the prevailing MOSI evaluation practice.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A7.SS4.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Baselines.</h5>

<div id="A7.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To situate our method among representative approaches, we compare against widely cited MSA baselines that span tensor fusion, low-rank factorization, recurrent and deep feed-forward fusion, graph-based memory models, and cross-modal transformers. Below we list each baseline with its canonical citation (the superscripts indicate the source of numbers when we report them in tables: <sup id="A7.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_sup"><span id="A7.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">†</span></sup> from THUIAR’s GitHub/toolkit, <sup id="A7.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_sup"><span id="A7.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">∗</span></sup> from the original paper, and <sup id="A7.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.3" class="ltx_sup"><span id="A7.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">∗∗</span></sup> reproduced by us with released code/hyperparameters):</p>
<ul id="A7.I2" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="A7.I2.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A7.I2.i1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.I2.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A7.I2.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">TFN<sup id="A7.I2.i1.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_sup"><span id="A7.I2.i1.p1.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">†</span></sup></span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib33" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zadeh et al., 2017</a>)</cite>:
Tensor Fusion Network introducing explicit multimodal tensor interactions.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A7.I2.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A7.I2.i2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.I2.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A7.I2.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">LMF<sup id="A7.I2.i2.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_sup"><span id="A7.I2.i2.p1.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">∗</span></sup></span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib34" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al., 2018</a>)</cite>:
Low-Rank Multimodal Fusion reducing TFN’s cubic complexity via factorization.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A7.I2.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A7.I2.i3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.I2.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A7.I2.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">EF-LSTM<sup id="A7.I2.i3.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_sup"><span id="A7.I2.i3.p1.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">†</span></sup></span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib31" title="" class="ltx_ref">Williams et al., 2018b</a>)</cite>:
Early-fusion recurrent model that concatenates modalities prior to sequence modeling.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A7.I2.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A7.I2.i4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.I2.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A7.I2.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">LF-DNN<sup id="A7.I2.i4.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_sup"><span id="A7.I2.i4.p1.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">†</span></sup></span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib32" title="" class="ltx_ref">Williams et al., 2018a</a>)</cite>:
Late-fusion deep network combining modality-specific predictors at the decision level.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A7.I2.i5" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A7.I2.i5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.I2.i5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A7.I2.i5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Graph-MFN<sup id="A7.I2.i5.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_sup"><span id="A7.I2.i5.p1.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">†</span></sup></span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib35" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zadeh et al., 2018</a>)</cite>:
Graph-structured Memory Fusion Network for cross-view temporal reasoning.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A7.I2.i6" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A7.I2.i6.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.I2.i6.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A7.I2.i6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">MulT<sup id="A7.I2.i6.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_sup"><span id="A7.I2.i6.p1.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">∗</span></sup></span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib36" title="" class="ltx_ref">Tsai et al., 2019</a>)</cite>:
Cross-modal Transformer that performs directional attention across modalities.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A7.I2.i7" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A7.I2.i7.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.I2.i7.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A7.I2.i7.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">MISA<sup id="A7.I2.i7.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_sup"><span id="A7.I2.i7.p1.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">†</span></sup></span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib37" title="" class="ltx_ref">Hazarika et al., 2020</a>)</cite>:
Modality-Invariant/Specific representations with contrastive objectives to disentangle factors.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A7.I2.i8" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A7.I2.i8.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.I2.i8.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A7.I2.i8.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">ICCN<sup id="A7.I2.i8.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_sup"><span id="A7.I2.i8.p1.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">∗</span></sup></span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib39" title="" class="ltx_ref">Sun et al., 2020</a>)</cite>:
Cross-modal correlation networks leveraging canonical correlation constraints.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A7.I2.i9" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A7.I2.i9.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.I2.i9.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A7.I2.i9.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">DLF<sup id="A7.I2.i9.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_sup"><span id="A7.I2.i9.p1.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">∗∗</span></sup></span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib40" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2025</a>)</cite>:
A recent strong multimodal baseline emphasizing deep latent fusion.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A7.I2.i10" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A7.I2.i10.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.I2.i10.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A7.I2.i10.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">ALMT<sup id="A7.I2.i10.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_sup"><span id="A7.I2.i10.p1.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">∗∗</span></sup></span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib38" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhang et al., 2023</a>)</cite>:
Attention-based latent model trained with MSE; we use ALMT as the host architecture for our ECA augmentation.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A7.SS4.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Implementation.</h5>

<div id="A7.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Unless otherwise noted, we follow the standard MOSI preprocessing and the train/validation/test partition described above. For baselines, we adhere to the configuration choices recommended by the original authors or by THUIAR’s toolkit <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib29" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yu et al., 2020</a>; <a href="#bib.bib28" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yu et al., 2021</a>)</cite>. Our primary report includes <span id="A7.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_markedasmath">F1</span>, <span id="A7.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_markedasmath">PCC</span>, and <span id="A7.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_markedasmath">MAE</span> on the held-out test set, with validation used solely for early stopping and hyperparameter selection. The model training is with 2 A6000 GPUs.</p>
</div>
<div id="A7.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We adopt ALMT as the base architecture and keep the optimizer and data pipeline fixed across all runs to ensure a clean ablation. We train for 100 epochs with a batch size of 64, using AdamW with lr=1e-4 and batching and loading use num_workers=8. Other hyperparameters are shown in <a href="#A7.T5" title="In Implementation. ‣ G.4 Multimodal Sentiment Analysis (MSA) Dataset ‣ Appendix G Detailed Experimental Settings ‣ Breaking the Correlation Plateau: On the Optimization and Capacity Limits of Attention-Based Regressors" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A7.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p3.1" class="ltx_p">ALMT, in its original form, is trained with MSE loss only. To probe correlation-aware training and our correlation-aware aggregation, we evaluate two controlled settings (all other hyperparameters are held constant):</p>
</div>
<div id="A7.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<ol id="A7.I3" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="A7.I3.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="A7.I3.i1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.I3.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A7.I3.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">ALMT + PCC loss (no architectural change).</span>
We augment the training objective with a differentiable PCC term, yielding a weighted sum</p>
<table id="A7.Ex28" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A7.Ex28.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}\;=\;\lambda_{\text{MSE}}\cdot\mathrm{MSE}\;+\;\lambda_{\text{PCC}}\cdot\mathcal{L}_{\text{PCC}}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mo lspace="0.558em" rspace="0.558em">=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mtext>MSE</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mi>MSE</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0.502em" rspace="0.502em">+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mtext>PCC</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>PCC</mtext></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}\;=\;\lambda_{\text{MSE}}\cdot\mathrm{MSE}\;+\;\lambda_{\text{PCC}}\cdot\mathcal{L}_{\text{PCC}},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A7.I3.i1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A7.I3.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda_{\text{MSE}}{=}1.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mtext>MSE</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1.0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_{\text{MSE}}{=}1.0</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A7.I3.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda_{\text{PCC}}{=}1.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mtext>PCC</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1.0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_{\text{PCC}}{=}1.0</annotation></semantics></math>.
This setting isolates the effect of explicitly encouraging high Pearson correlation during training while leaving the model architecture unchanged.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A7.I3.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="A7.I3.i2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.I3.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A7.I3.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">ALMT + PCC loss + ECA (ours).</span>
In addition to the above loss, we adopt our proposed ECA method in the vision stream by modifying the ViT-style token aggregation step.</p>
</div></li>
</ol>
</div>
<figure id="A7.T5" class="ltx_table">

<section id="A7.SS4.SSS0.Px5" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Extra Results Analysis.</h5>

<div id="A7.SS4.SSS0.Px5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS4.SSS0.Px5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">By comparing Setting 1 to the MSE-only ALMT, we measure the gain from correlation-aware training alone. Comparing Setting 2 to Setting 1 isolates the benefit of ECA’s vision-token aggregation. As summarized in Table <a href="#S5.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ 5.2 Results and analysis ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ Breaking the Correlation Plateau: On the Optimization and Capacity Limits of Attention-Based Regressors" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>, adding PCC improves correlation-oriented metrics without harming classification quality, and coupling PCC with our ECA aggregation <em id="A7.SS4.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">further</em> improves all three metrics (F1, PCC, MAE). These results indicate that ECA enhances the multimodal pipeline beyond loss-level changes, demonstrating tangible benefits for <em id="A7.SS4.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">multimodality</em> on MOSI.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A8" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix H </span>Batch Size Effect on PCC Plateau</h2>

<div id="A8.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A8.p1.1" class="ltx_p">A potential concern regarding the joint optimization of MSE and PCC is whether the batch size <math id="A8.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>S</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S</annotation></semantics></math> influences the optimization dynamics, specifically the onset of the PCC plateau. Theoretically, as discussed in <a href="#S2.SS3" title="2.3 Optimization Dynamics: The Correlation Gradient Bottleneck ‣ 2 Theoretical Analysis of Correlation Learning in Attention-based Aggregation ‣ Breaking the Correlation Plateau: On the Optimization and Capacity Limits of Attention-Based Regressors" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.3</span></a> and the <a href="#S2.E6" title="In Corollary 2.1 (PCC/MSE Gradient Ratio Decay). ‣ Gradient Decomposition and the Optimization Conflict. ‣ 2.3 Optimization Dynamics: The Correlation Gradient Bottleneck ‣ 2 Theoretical Analysis of Correlation Learning in Attention-based Aggregation ‣ Breaking the Correlation Plateau: On the Optimization and Capacity Limits of Attention-Based Regressors" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Equation</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>, both the MSE and PCC gradient magnitudes scale proportionally with <math id="A8.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1/S" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>S</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1/S</annotation></semantics></math>. Consequently, the ratio between the two gradients that determines the effective optimization direction is invariant to the batch size. This suggests that the conflict causing the plateau is fundamental to the gradient properties (specifically the <math id="A8.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1/\sigma_{\hat{y}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><msub><mi>σ</mi><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1/\sigma_{\hat{y}}</annotation></semantics></math> attenuation) and the homogeneous PCC bound, rather than batch statistics.</p>
</div>
<div id="A8.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A8.p2.1" class="ltx_p">To empirically validate this independence, we conducted an ablation study using the synthetic dataset described in <a href="#S5.SS1" title="5.1 Experimental Setup ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ Breaking the Correlation Plateau: On the Optimization and Capacity Limits of Attention-Based Regressors" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.1</span></a>, training the standard attention regression model with varying batch sizes <math id="A8.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S\in\{32,64,128\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>32</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>64</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>128</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S\in\{32,64,128\}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A8.F10" class="ltx_figure ltx_align_center">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 10: </span>MSE and PCC curve under various batch size settings.</figcaption>
</figure>
<figure id="A8.fig1" class="ltx_figure ltx_align_center"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2602.17898v1/batch_32.svg" id="A8.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:548/354;" width="548" height="354"></object>
</figure>
<figure id="A8.fig2" class="ltx_figure ltx_align_center"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2602.17898v1/batch_64.svg" id="A8.g2" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:548/353;" width="548" height="353"></object>
</figure>
<figure id="A8.fig3" class="ltx_figure ltx_align_center"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2602.17898v1/batch_128.svg" id="A8.g3" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:548/354;" width="548" height="354"></object>
</figure>
<div id="A8.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A8.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><a href="#A8" title="Appendix H Batch Size Effect on PCC Plateau ‣ Breaking the Correlation Plateau: On the Optimization and Capacity Limits of Attention-Based Regressors" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">H</span></a> presents the learning curves for these settings. The results align with our theoretical analysis:</p>
<ul id="A8.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="A8.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A8.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A8.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A8.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Consistent Plateau Behavior:</span> Across all batch sizes, we observe the characteristic decoupling of the metrics. The PCC curves (red) flatten and plateau significantly earlier than the MSE curves (blue), which continue to decrease steadily throughout training.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A8.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A8.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A8.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Generalization Gap:</span> Both training (dashed) and validation (solid) curves exhibit similar trends, indicating that this phenomenon is an optimization issue rather than a generalization issue.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
<div id="A8.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A8.p4.1" class="ltx_p">These results confirm that increasing or decreasing the batch size does not resolve the PCC plateau, further validating the necessity of the architectural interventions proposed in our ECA to explicitly counteract gradient attenuation.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A9" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix I </span>Disclosure of LLM Usage</h2>

<div id="A9.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A9.p1.1" class="ltx_p">A large language model (LLM) was used only for language refinement (grammar, phrasing, and clarity) in the main paper and the appendix. The LLM did not contribute to the research ideas, mathematical derivations, theorems, proofs, or experimental design. All technical content was independently produced and reviewed by the authors.</p>
</div>
</section>
</article>
